review_text: We really enjoyed our 3D/2N tour from San Pedro to Uyuni. Booking was easy and clear as Raül in the office spoke very good English to us. We were explained the route carefully and given an itinerary. If you pay in USD make sure they’re in good condition or mint, as they won’t accept any worn notes. We were picked up promptly when Cruz said, and the van was a spacious new van with 12 people in total. As the border near San Pedro was closed due to snow, we had to take a detour 3 hours north to the Ollagüe border. The border crossing at Chile was slow due to several tour groups, but easy. The driver remained with us for this and made sure we all got stamped ok. Passing through Bolivian border was super fast, our passports stamped in no time, and we were transferred to the 4x4’s and set off. It’s worth agreeing with your fellow passengers to rotate in the 4x4s as the back seats are a little cramped. The food provided was good quality, and we were catered for well being vegetarians. Breakfast was usually bread, cheese, spreads, cake, biscuits, tea, coffee. Lunches were pasta, rice, vegetables, potato bakes, salads, etc. Dinner the second night was excellent and we got some Bolivian wine too. Maybe take some snacks with you and plenty of water in case you get peckish along the way as there aren’t any stops for supplies. The sights we saw were incredible, some of the best in 9 months of backpacking. We saw mountains, valleys, flamingos, llamas, lagoons, canyons, which was all in addition to the salt plains on the last day. Our driver Andreas was very careful, professional and told us little snippets about places along the way. He spoke basic English but we had a Spanish speaking passenger translating for us in the car. He was always asking us to play music, and stopping regularly for photos. He was super chilled, wanted us to see a range of things and a genuinely nice guy. The accommodation on the first night was basic but fine. We asked for sleeping bags when booking which helped massively as it was absolutely freezing. Plenty of blankets on the bed as well. The bathrooms weren’t the cleanest, and some showers were not warm but we got on with it, knowing the second night would be better. The Salt hotel on night 2 was super cute, well insulated en suite rooms with hot water (one person showering at a time!) There were only a couple of small matters which were a little disappointing. Firstly communication wasn’t the best as once we paid for the tour, that was when we were told the border near San Pedro had been closed due to the snow so there may be an alternative route. It would have been better to inform us of the potential new route in advance of paying. We wouldn’t have changed our minds as any other tour group would be in the same situation, but as it remained closed, we went the alternative route which meant we missed out the red lake and the geysers (the geysers were actually closed due to the weather). Apparently the red lake was frozen over too so consider this if you’re going in winter. Secondly, dinner the first night was extremely disappointing as we were served pasta with a very small dish of sauce to share, and the non-vegetarians got a very small piece of meat too. We were all starving as we had lunch early, and dinner was served after 8pm. As all the other meals were substantial, I can only hope this was a one off. Some of the stops listed on the itinerary we didn’t not go to, but there were some stops we visited which weren’t on the itinerary. This was not much of an issue as everything we saw was absolutely incredible. If you’re specific about what you want to see then maybe speak to the driver to make sure you don’t miss out. Overall this tour was excellent, we loved it. We would definitely recommend Cruz Andina and Andreas our driver. We just would have liked clarification on the border situation before booking.

review_text: My wife and I stayed at Chepu Adventures during the third week in December. Southern Chile is in the middle of one of the rainiest 10 day periods in recent history. All of the locals were shaking their heads at the unusual weather. At any other resort this type of weather could have cast a real dark spell on the scene. Not at Chepu Adventures. The owners Amory and Fernando were wonderful with making sure that ALL of their guests needs were attended to.We managed to get a couple of kayak trips up the river in during our stay, but a lot of our time was spent socializing with other " Eco" guests at the lodge. The rooms are very comfortable and clean and the dinners that Amory prepared were very good. The owners take care to make all of their guests feel at home and understand the history and the reality of living in a remote and fragile environment. Even with the wet weather we had a great time ; I can only imagine how great it would have been in warm weather.

review_text: Where to start? Juane arranged two adventure-filled and wine-packed days for us while we were in town. To begin, an amazing and informative driver picked us up from the airport and transported us to our accommodation. He toured us around town a bit, pointing out the major attractions as we passed them by. The next morning Juane arrived to take us on our day hike in the hills of the Andes. It was so much fun, the scenery was amazing and Juane knew the route like the back of his hand. We crossed the rapids, drank from a stream, and had an incredible spread at the end of the hike that included avocado, tomato, meats and cheese, and the most amazing bread (and a bit of wine, because we were obviously dehydrated,ha!) The next day Juane picked us up once more and this time took us to the Casablanca wine region where he'd set up two amazing bodega tours as well as brunch. The tours were informative and the tastings were incredible. Great scenery and even better company. Juane also arranged our transport from Vina del Mar to the airport. Honestly, we had the most fun and I'm so glad I stumbled upon this tour group. I can't imagine having anyone else plan and accompany us on our trip. When we make it back to Chile, I'm certain I'll use their services again and I recommend them highly, completely to take care of any tour needs you'd have while in the area. Simply, the best! Hi Holly, Thank you for booking with us! We are so happy to hear you and your friends had such a good time! Juane also had a blast with you girls! See you on your next trip to Chile!

review_text: We arrived in Santiago on Tuesday, almost midnight. We had the entire itinerary planned and Wednesday was free, however, the agency sent a message that the tour on Thursday (Portillo) would be closed and moved us to Wednesday, we approved the change because they have greater knowledge of things. Okay, tired and almost sleepless because at 5 something in the morning the van came to pick us up, we went, it had already been reported that the road would be closed on Wednesday/Thursday and even so the agency sent the entire van there to waste time, we arrived in Santiago again, almost 13 hours and as if that wasn't enough, the driver who had a non-defensive driving style committed traffic violations, being stopped by the police and making us lose another 1 hour! He even told us to walk back to the apartment! Yes…you hire a well-rated agency because you want security/peace of mind and need to go through such embarrassment. The next day, we went for the “Andes Panoramic” tour, but halfway through we discovered that it was the “Sky Day” tour, we had no intention of going sky, I sent a message to the saleswoman who responded hours later informing me that the tour Panoramic, it wouldn't happen that day, however, I was already in the new van on the way to this same tour and it would happen! (I really didn't understand her stance). Thank you, guide Vitor, for responding promptly and solving the problem for us! I just didn't give it one star because my evaluation is based on reliable experience and the guides Vitor, Sol and Alexandro and also the driver Emerson provided me with a great service! Thanks! As for the 2 incidents, the agency showed no intention of compensating me, apologizing, etc. Obviously when you travel the last thing you want is for a situation like the one described above to occur in order to obtain advantages or discounts, but they acted as if this was normal, so I was very scared! And there is no money that can pay for 1 lost day of a trip planned for a long time, anyone who plans knows…. Imagine being a person with an anxiety attack, being in another country and being in a van with 5 police officers interrogating the driver and you there without knowing anything or anyone on your first day! Total horror! EVERYTHING could have been avoided if the agency hadn't sent the van on the day the tour was closed! But in the end it must have been a relief not to have climbed 29 mountain bends with a reckless driver!

review_text: Our guide Thomas was our guide on a day trip to Cajon del Maipo. We were picked up at our downtown hotel promptly as promised. There were a total of 4 passengers on our tour. We stopped for hot chocolate and blueberry cake on the drive up. The river, reservoir, and snowcapped mountains were beautiful, and a lunch of snacks and wine was provided at a scenic spot by the reservoir. Our only recommendation would be for the tour company to clean the van windows more thoroughly in the morning.

review_text: We booked this tour as it was rated no.1 on Trip Advisor, and probably is, as we have no other comparison, and it was fun and interesting. Jorge is super enthusiastic and it's just unbelievable to see all the stars and milky way, and he explains everything with a lot of passion - the location is priceless. However, it was pricey and to be honest, I think we'd have enjoyed it more, if it had been half as long (we were there for three hours) and half the cost. Also, having more basic instructions on how to spot the constellations etc would have been nice, rather than the more advanced info and history lesson that was given. There was lots of gazing (naturally) through telescopes, but unless you really know your stuff, it is a little too much for someone who just likes looking up and wants to know roughly which star you're looking at. We found the 3 hours a long time - especially when you're tired from having done other activities in the day - I guess Jorge is just so passionate, that it was hard to gauge the tiredness of the group, and as a few there were really into it, it went on for a bit too long. However, that said, we did enjoy it and appreciated his passion, and the photos and his help in getting the settings right, and the hot chocolate is as lovely as everyone says! Dear Sona, Thank you very much for your review. Perhaps the tour you needed take it was TAT because SAT 1 is for advanced watcher and if you wanted to watch more time the night sky without a long astronomy class TAT is shorter and more time to observe the classic objets and price looks high compare with other similar companies but everyone that take the tour pay the knowledges that I know and give them. Anyway we felt very happy that you took the tour with us. Best Regards Jorge Corante F.

review_text: Santiago is not prepared for bicycles on public streets. They are more dangerous then motorcycles for the lack of visability of car drivers. One crept up on me when waiting for a stop light. I put on my blinker to turn left, did not check my right rearview mirror, being unaccustomed to bikes in the area and to my horror ran into him! Neither car drivers nor roads in Santiago are prepared for this invasion of bikes. It is more dangerous than motorcycles. The city is beginning to make stretches of bike paths but it has a century to go to get up to Holland's standards. Biking in parks is another story. The Bicentennial Park, over 53 hectares, has a bike rental stand at the beginning of the south end. It has lovely bike paths weaving through the park in safety and with plenty of room for bikers to enjoy. Paul McCarthy rents a bike there when he comes to Santiago to not only for the exercise but also to enjoy the view, a lovely contrast with the Andes to the north and a cosmopolitan city to the south with its sky scrapers. The park also has paths for joggers. The park is a stone throw away from the Airbnb B&B rental called "Magical Views". The park as a children's area with jungle gyms etc apart so that children don't bother those using the park for other reasons. It is a visit for all types, couples, families with little children, growing children, friends, perhaps for business reasons? but as per the other options its a great place for those who want to be alone. One can spend an hour or a day. Its a great place not only for working out, picnics are discretely held around the thousands of Chilean trees dispersed throughout the park.

review_text: We spent 3 days rafting this wild river in this unbelievably beautiful location. At the very start of the season, Bochinche was the only operator that offered us a multi-day rafting adventure, covering pretty much every main rapid the Futaleufu has to offer: Terminator section, Puente a Puente section, El Macal section. Our local guide, Daniel, knew the river like the back of his hand and has 10+ years of experience guiding trips all over the world. The river is powerful and the high class rapids are technical, he takes the time to explain each section before we start and really draws you in the adventure. We had some rainy days and the water levels were high, but the team did everything to adapt our trip to the conditions in a safe way, i.e. reshuffling some of the sections, changing the start time, bringing along extra safety kayaks, etc. I'm confident no other operator would have given us the same experience. As for safety, every trip had at least one safety kayak and cataraft accompanying our raft. At the end of the third day, Daniel and Giorgia invited us to their home for a great asado with the other guides. After a couple of days on the river, we definitely felt connected, and truly welcomed. An unforgettable experience, thanks a lot! Hi Maarten and thanks a lot for your comment. It was great meeting and getting to know you guys and a pleasure showing you the amazing Futaleufu river. We hope to see you soon for another extraordinary adventure!!!

review_text: I arrived in Pucon around 8:15 after an overnight bus from Santiago and checked into my hostel. Since it was too late to do the Volcano trek (6:30) and I had missed the earlier bus to Huerquehue National Park, this was an ideal alternative as there are very regular buses to and from the Santuario and I didn't want to waste a day hanging around the hostel and town (not that either were bad). I took a bus around 10:15, which arrived about half an hour later (its the bus station opposite the JAC terminal around the corner from Pullman). I just mentioned El Cani and jumped on the right bus, the driver should shout when you get to the spot. A brief walk and you need to pop into the hut they have and pay entrance (3,000 pesos I think / 6 dollars) and you get a basic map that one of the guys write on (there is a check point further up where you may or may not have to show this (I didn't...un-manned). In all honesty, the first part of the hike up to the refugio is very dull and not particularly fun (dirt tracks). The map indicates about 2 hours to get there albeit I did it in almost half the time as I was on a bit of a mission that day and ran a little. After the refugio the hike got a reasonable amount easier as you start heading to the lakes. The lakes were a big disappointment for me being perfectly honest. The first was almost completely dried up and the second was quite small and also part dried. From the second lake however, you start a tough 30 minute ascent to the mirador (viewing point), and believe me, that was worth it. The views from the top are pretty spectacular, with three volcanoes in the distance (including Villarica of course). Its pretty clear up there and there are plenty of rocks to perch yourself and rest your tired feet whilst munching a few snacks. I actually got to the top in two and half hours so it can be done a lot quicker than indicated. Whilst parts of the above sound quite negative, the view really is fantastic and I imagine the rest of the park would be much better out of peak summer time when the lakes have more water, or when the trees are covered in snow. The other additional bonus is that most people go to Huerquehue and so you practically have it to yourself (I was the first person in the park even at 10:45). Well worth a visit, especially for the more budget conscious seeking a panoramic view.

review_text: We visited Antilco back in February, but it was such an amazing experience I needed time to ensure the review did Mathias and Karin justice. My husband and I spent a week staying in their beautiful wooden cabin, with 4 days of riding (2 half days and a 2 day trek) alongside 5 mornings of studying Spanish with Karin. We couldn’t have had a better introduction to Chile. It was such a perfect combination as Mathias organised the horse riding on his ranch whilst his wife runs a language school in Pucón. We barely knew any Spanish before leaving England and after a week of studying at Antilco we left with a good foundation of Spanish for the rest of our month exploring Patagonia. We hired a car for 10 days and had great fun picking up hitch hikers to ensure we kept practising! The horse riding was absolutely incredible and the ultimate highlight was the 2 day trek into the mountains. It was such a dream come true to go camping under the most amazing stars, travelling by horse. The food provided on the camping trip was delicious and we will never forget cooking the steaks over the fire under the stars. We would highly recommend Antilco and Lingua Plus for horse riding and/or learnings spanish. We really hope to return in the future for a 4 day horse trek as this really was our highlight from a month exploring Chile. A huge thanks to Mathias, Karin, our 2 guides and of course the horses who looked after us over the 4 days of riding Polka, Moro, Sombra and Bonita.

review_text: I enjoyed a really nice small-group tour with Central Tours to the Elqui Valley, the highlights being the Puclaro Dam & reservoir, the Gabriela Mistral museum in Vicuna, a pisco distillery, and a nice lunch in Pisco Elqui. There were other short stops for scenic lookouts and small towns, and we did some walking but nothing too strenuous. Some were just quick stops that allowed us to get out and stretch our legs and snap a few photos, without hanging around too long. I felt it was very well paced overall. Our guide was Sebastian, who was very knowledgeable about the area. It is certainly a scenic ride, but he really made it come alive with information about the local history, natural resources, and social aspects. The rest of the group was Spanish-speaking, but Sebastian is completely bi-lingual, and immediately offered to give the tour in both languages. I told him it wouldn’t be necessary, and I was able to follow most of his commentary, but nevertheless he kept checking in with me in English throughout the day to be sure I understood. And if he would point out something quickly as we drove by it, he made sure to get my attention, as well. That is a real sign of a quality guide, in my opinion. One note – their web site is only in Spanish (maybe they’ll have English translations soon?), and my first call to them wasn’t a very good cell connection. But they got back in touch with me quickly on WhatsApp in English (which I prefer when making arrangements), and were able to accommodate me on short notice. I would recommend Central Tours without hesitation.

review_text: All the rave reviews of this tour are all true, and Daniel is a gem of a guide!! Daniel is not your typical guide. He genuinely loves art and culture and he is passionate in what he does and we believe he wants the best for his clients (sounds weird since I don't think he views us as his clients -- we are more like his friends!!). His tour truly stands out from other Valparaiso tours. I compared most of the Valparaiso tours on TripAdvisor, and his is the only one that allows flexibility and focuses on the art and culture aspects of what Valparaiso offers. Our tour took place on NYD (today)!!! This is what Daniel described as a "hard holiday" meaning things are closed and his employees are not available (he worked as our driver and our guide) so the question is should he still offer the tour while running the risk of disappointing his "clients?" We were very lucky because he did!! And he was very transparent and honest with us about the limitations of touring on NYD and what he could or could not do!! We did not do the wine tasting part of the tour since the vineyard was closed (which was just fine). Instead we did an in-depth tour of Valparaiso, and it was truly memorable. review_text: We originally booked the Maipo tour but was emailed 1 day prior to advise that the route had been closed to tourists due to an accident. They then offered us the Portillo tour instead, claiming that it was twice the cost and we would still see lots of mountains. The first stop was to the snow clothing hire shop. We were convinced it was going to be a lot colder and the tour guide recommended that we dress accordingly. Our hire came to a total of $86aud for pants, gloves and snow boots for 2 people. Only to find out when we arrived to the mountain that they were not necessary. We then were taken to a snow area on the side of the highway to play in the snow. We were told that the ski resort would be too crowded and this would be a good time to get photos etc. As most of the bus was from Brazil, our tour guide spoke mostly in Portuguese, translating to English every now and then. However when we arrived to the ski resort at midday, our understanding was that we were to spend and hour and a half at the resort and have lunch at the restaurant. The guide took a list of names who were wanting to go to the restaurant as we were told that the hotel only wanted paying customers at the resort. The food was terrible and overpriced. We paid $70aud for 2 meals and the meat was so over cooked, it could be cut or chewed. This was quite disappointing considering how much we paid and even though we bought lunch, we were not allowed to use the bathrooms. We were told that these were for hotel guests only. The resort is a bit of let down also, there’s not much to do, other than take photos in one designated area for tourists. When we arrived back to the bus, we were told that we would drive for another hour and half to take back the snow gear and then have lunch! We approached the driver and told him we thought he asked us to have lunch here. There was another English speaking person on the bus and she too had lunch at the resort from the guides instructions. Clearly something was lost in translation. The food at the lunch spot was half the price too and looked much more appetising. We were very disappointed. Overall I would not recommend this tour to anyone. It was boring and we ended up paying more on the day then we did the tour cost. Review of: Small-Group Tour of Portillo Ski Center and Inca Lagoon from Santiago

review_text: Fort Bulnes is a historic fort built on a point that juts out into the Straits of Magellan. Dating back to the 1800s, it's been restored a number of times, but is now part of a newly opened state park. The visitors' center houses exhibits on the area, and had just opened a few weeks prior to my visit. While a number of the exhibits were still unfinished I thought it was well presented and the views from the center were exceptional. The real reason make the 45 minute drive from Punta Arenas is that there's no one else out there. We were just about the only car on the road headed to the park and back, and less than a handful of people were in the park. There are great trails and lookouts throughout the point with spectacular views of the Straits. We had it all to ourselves except for the dolphins that passed by for a look too.

review_text: My wife Judy and I met FredaTopolosky in Holland America's Zaandam laundry, we were very lucky. Why? Because Freda had trolled the Internet and found out about the Nao Victoria Museum and with her husband Bruce, invited Judy and I to join them on a visit. We disembarked from the Zaandam at Punta Arenas, using tenders, and then went through Chilean immigration and customs. The four of us then muscled into an impossibly small taxi for the four mile journey to the musem, easily located on the right hand side of the main road in the eastern part of the city. What did we find? First of all we met a delightful father and son who, between themselves, had built a beautifulful full size replica of Magellan's Nao Victoria, one of five ships that left Spain in September 1519 to sail around the world. We were able to climb into Nao Victoria and marvel at the skill of Magellan's navigation and seamanship, and the toughness of the crew. Of the 42 crewmembers that set sail from Sanlucar (near today's Gibraltar),19 survived to return to Spain almost exactly three years later. Under construction is a replica of the famous British ship, HMS Beagle which, on its second voyage around the world, took scientist Charles Darwin to the Falkland Islands, Punta Arenas and then onwards through the Magellan Strait and up along the Chilean coast to the Galapogos. This replica construction will be completed by the end of 2015. Also worth viewing is a replica of the sloop that enabled explorer Ernest Shackleton and some of his crew to escape Antartica in appalling weather. Sadly, none of the Punta Arenas promotional material mentions this museum, it is well worth a visit, children and adults will be fascinated to climb into a 500 year old ship and to view things like the amazing steering system which was also used on the Mayflower.

review_text: Neruda is both poet and social conscious of Chile. His architectural tastes and aesthetic are interesting, but not all of his houses are created equal. He has three you can tour: downtown Santiago, in the Bellavista neighborhood; Valparaiso; and Isla Negra, south of Valparaiso and accessible by cab or bus. The house at Valparaiso is the least interesting of the three. The Neruda house in Santiago is an excellent introduction as is the house just south of Valparaiso, at Isla Negra. The Santiago house has the most interesting furnishings and architectural styling (Neruda was fascinated by the sea, and the rooms in Santiago are very reflective of that). The furnishings and artifacts at the Valparaiso house are less interesting and less typical of his style. The Valparaiso house is currently under renovation, so the third floor is closed. At the very least, until the entire Valparaiso house is open, I'd give it a pass, unless you are a serious Neruda fan.It's a bit out of the way, and ti's not particularly cheap, and likely to disappoint. Visit the houses as Isla Negra or Santiago instead.

review_text: I had this dream of going to Torres del Paine for over 25 years. I've always thought this place was sort of a mythical place, one of those natural wonders you find only in movies. The place is filled with civilized outposts and trekkers, so you won't find it hard to cross with people either to get directions or any kind of support or stimulation. In general all people I've met were generous, life-lovers and well-intentioned fellows. review_text: Arriving early in the morning before the crowds, me and my sister bought coffee from a local man selling espresso out of a small cart and sat down by the pier and watched the waves ripple across Lake Llanquihue. Frutillar doesn't have much to do, but that's kind of the beauty of it. After we finished our drinks, we wandered around town admiring the unique architecture in the town. Homes in Frutillar and the Lake District in general fuse Germanic elements with characteristically Latin color combinations on what would otherwise be run-of-the-mill buildings. Keep your eye out for the music school which has forest green corrugated metal siding with ornate wooden window frames. It is definitely worth spending some time exploring this small German colony! To get here, take the mini busses going down Av San Francisco in Puerto Varas. Hop on any one that says "Frutillar Bajo." It costs CLP$1000 and takes about an hour each way.

Rolling her son, she allowed herself to be defeated, but not her granddaughter Romina, with her husband Angel. Today, they have great rooms, dressed and equipped with taste and comfort. There are no televisions, which invites quiet reading listening to the river. Owners collaborate with state institutions and universities in volcanological studies and preserve the ecosystem. A piece of paradise on earth... Hopefully we can come back!!!!

review_text: This pier has been significantly updated since the last review was posted here on Trip Advisor. It now hosts a wide variety of water sport activities for people of all ages. Here you can rent kayaks, stand-up paddle boards, and small sailboats. You can receive instruction in all these activities, and I also saw people doing scuba diving (not sure if there is instruction for that). It is also accessible for people in wheelchairs, and we saw a gentleman in a wheelchair on a paddle board out by himself out on the water! We have twice rented small sailboats here (about 4 meters long). I have zero experience sailing so if I can do this, anyone can. They have captains who go out with you and explain how to sail the boat while they take you around Valparaíso Bay. If you want, you can try your hand at the rudder and help with the sails. As I understand it, the wind comes up in the afternoon so it's best to do this at 1:00 pm or later. Of course they give you life jackets and they even had sunscreen if you forgot your own. The sailing lasts about 2 hours, you have fantastic views of the city and the huge cargo ships, not to mention sea lions and lots of birds. For the 2 hour trip with captain, they charge CLP $35.000 - you can fit up to four people on the boat and the captain makes 5 total. The pier also has several restaurants and an enormous sign that says "VALPARAISO" that is a must-have photo opp for any tourist coming to the city. Access to the pier is a bit tricky due to a lot of construction in the area, but you enter near the "Barón" metro station and follow the signs. I would call this a must-stop for anyone who likes the water and wants to do something a little out-of-the-ordinary

The guide was knowledgeable and provided a good introduction to the basics of the history of Chile, including a very balanced and rational description of the turbulent 70's. The tour does not go into the buildings, but shows you the outside and talks about them, so that you can come back and visit. The four hours pass very fast, and you get a coffee/beer stop in the middle. The tour is free, but you are expected to tip the guide, I would recommend at least US$10.

I'd recommend a trip to the geysers, particularly if you haven't previously seen any.

review_text: I was only able to visit a small portion of this sprawling metropolitan park so I can only speak to this experience. The views from atop are great and there are a plethora of amenities (food vendors, cafes and restaurants along the top). The venue is family friendly and overrun with tourists, locals and cyclists who are either labouring up the winding roads or zooming down the pathways and designated trails. To get to the top you can either walk or bike (5-6km) up the various roads and trails or take the busy funicular up. The funicular round trip for an adult is $2,600 CLP. Be prepared to wait 30 minutes to an hour to get to the top and then again to get back down. Once at the top you can walk along to the Japanese botanical garden or take the scenic gondola across to the next peak for an extra fee. Budget at least 2-3 hours for the visit but you can easily spend there the whole day exploring.

review_text: My wife and I recently visited Chile. Family found a website for Hec Tour Service who advertised tours suitable for disabled persons. My wife who owns a Travel Agency in Taradale, New Zealand, is wheelchair bound so we decided to contact Hec Tour Service to ascertain if they could provide us with a suitable tour that would also cater for my wife’s needs. I mailed Hec Tour Service through their trip advisor link late on the Thursday evening and received a very prompt reply. After further communications Hec Tour Service confirmed a private tour on the Friday at 1100 am. They collected us from our accommodation promptly on time at 1100 am with an English-speaking tour guide. The guide was wonderful – very polite and beautifully spoken. We were transported in an excellent modern car and taken on a wonderful tour through several of Valparaiso’s delightful and charming cerro’s (hills). We stopped for lunch at a very Chilean restaurant which our guide had told us had the best empanadas in Valpo. We were not disappointed – they were excellent, washed down by a pleasant cold Chilean cerveza. We were then taken through Vina del Mar and onto Concón. In summary we saw 3 greatly different locations during the tour – the eclectic beauty of Valparaiso, the modern of Vina del Mar, and the sandhills and awesome scenery of Concón. We were then returned to our hotel at the end of a wonderful day’s touring. The following day Hec Tour Services provided us with transportation within Valparaiso, again with the wonderful prompt and attentive service of the English-speaking guide. Hec Tour Service provided us with an experience way above our expectations and we will be delighted to recommend this company to any of my wife’s clients, or our friends, visiting Chile. Muchas gracias Hec Tour Service – a 5-star plus operation!

review_text: We did the Hueerquehue a los lagos, It is a 7 mi. rt hike that is moderately trafficked and mainly out and back with a small loop at the end. The hike includes about 2,000 feet of elevation gain. It is a lovely hike through woods with some views in the middle and at the end. We did it on a dry day which was good as it was not muddy. They say that people average about 5 hrs. It took us a little longer with several stops and a picnic at the top. Part of the drive to get there is on a bumpy dirt/gravel road. We did not have a four wheel car and made it fine, but a four wheel car with high clearance would be easier. Slight discount for those over 60.

review_text: February 2007 Outside Santiago, only a 45min drive on excellent highway for most of it, the delightful winery Vina Tarapaca ex Zavala is set in a sometimes misty Maipo valley surrounded by the Andes. And truly, a river runs through it. It's a beautiful setting with a delightful manor house that rumor says you can reserve a room at, though I've been unable to find it online. We were on a day trip from Santiago with a group. After driving past vine covered hillsides (with the occasional cactus) we arrived at the winery--first for a tour, and then for a wonderful lunch of grilled meats, salads, plenty of excellent wine, and delightful hospitality. The wines are very enjoyable--an excellent white, lovely Cab and very nice Carmenere . The grounds of the estate include sweeping mountain views over fields heavy with grapes, a very picturesque small church built for the winery workers, the winery facilities and an ivy-covered manor house, fountains and water garden, pool, small pitch and putt golf course, and grass airfield. It seems like it would be quite a nice romantic getaway for a weekend outside Santiago--very quiet. If you figure out how to book it, do post a link! I'd love to return as an overnight guest.

review_text: While visiting Santiago on business, I pondered what to do with my free time on the weekend. After looking through the options, I choose to take a tour of the Sewell Mining Town about 2.5 hours drive from Santiago. I went with a tour (TuristTour) and I think that is probably the only way to really get something from the experience. I choose this activity over the other options for two reasons: 1) to learn a little more about the economically vital copper mining industry in Chile and 2) to get out of the city and get up into the Andes mountains. This accomplished both. Our guide, Javiera, was very knowledgeable about the history of this town built into the mountain and even was able to explain a little bit about copper processing. We were able to stroll the town (it is not often I get to tromp through snow in July), walk through a couple of buildings and eat lunch with the mine employees in the cafeteria. This World Heritage site gives a good look at the mining industry and the life of the miners. The museum treated the subject of copper with a bit of a light overview but this is probably the best approach for the average tourist. On the other hand, it does a good job of showing the importance of copper to our everyday lives. The city is pretty amazing because it is like very few places you will see anywhere else. I also found out in talking with Javiera that the mine used to be private (as some of the displays in the museum suggested) but is now part of the state-run mining operation. She indicated that the mine was nationalized in the Allende era and this is a subject that I find deeply interesting. I had a very worthwhile off-line discussion with her concerning this subject. This is a matter about which many Chileans still display quite an uncomfortable reticence. Even if copper mining is a subject that holds little interest for you, this still represents a very important aspect of both Chilean history and its current economic vitality (Javiera indicated 40%+ of Chilean GDP is related to the mining industry). Being there and walking the town is a worthwhile experience. And the scenery to which you are exposed along the way is a major bonus.

review_text: We really enjoyed our tour of Santiago today. Franco was an excellent guide, with a perfect blend of historical/cultural understanding and humour. The whole tour took about 3.5 hours with a nice half hour stop at a restaurant (with no pressure to buy), but moved at a good pace and we didn't get the sense that any of the group of about 20 (aged from teens to seniors) were getting tired. review_text: I listened to the reviews on here and rented the audio guide (which I never do in a museum) and I'm glad I did since almost nothing was in English. The museum is free, but audio guide is CHP$2000. It's extremely convenient to the train station (Quinta Normal) and you don't even have to go outside. The museum is very detailed and powerful. To be honest, after visiting concentration camps in Germany and Poland, this one is much more mild, but nonetheless sheds light on a tumultuous time in Chilean History. I think it's a tribute to the people of Chile that this was built so relatively soon after the dictatorship. The strongest message is at the end - they tell the story so humans don't ever treat other humans that way. If only the rest of the world we live in felt that way.

review_text: My wife and I chose this tour based on the fact it looked the most authentic. A great decision!! The whole thing is run by Alex, his father Wilson, mother Clara and dog Angelito. A fantastic spread of hot drinks, snacks and homemade empanadas made by his mum was a nice touch. He even printed photos straight away for us as well as sending a heap through later on. A real bonus was Alex taking the time to give us a tutorial with our own camera around how to take high quality photos of the night sky. From start to finish this was one of the best experiences we have had in South America, genuine, authentic and enlightening. I would highly recommend Alex over a mainstream alternative anyday. review_text: This review is both for Kayak en Patagonia and its sister company, Fortaleza Expediciones . We did a 7 day hiking/kayaking trip that covered Torres del Paine National Park and Bernardo O'Higgins National Park in Patagonia. These places are indescribably beautiful, wild, thrilling and enthralling, and Fortaleza/Kayak en Patagonia provided the guide, gear, logistical support and food to make the trip seamless, stress-free, an information hound's dream, and a total blast. We did 3 days of hiking in Torres del Paine, and I highly recommend going in the low season - the weather was great and there were relatively few people on the trail. We stayed in the refugios on the hiking part of the trip, and they are all very nice and well-maintained. Absolutely gorgeous scenery. We had a very smooth transition to the 4-day kayaking part of the trip, with all the different gear miraculously appearing at our campsite just as we needed it, including our tents and dry suits. About the dry suits. They are really a stroke of genius on the owner's part. While we were kayaking the Grey and Serrano rivers, the weather changed constantly, from beautiful sunshine, to snow, to slanting rain, and back again - but it mattered not to us. With our dry suits and pogies we were able to paddle serenely along enjoying the scenery in all its glory without suffering from the wet or cold. Fantastic. Our guide Jose Luis was terrific. Knowledgeable, accomplished, capable and a great cook. On our final day he took us on an ice-breaking kayaking trip in the lake below Serrano glacier - a definite highlight of the trip. Along the way on the Serrano River we also camped on the land of a local rancher, and this proved another highlight of the trip. So if you're going all the way to Chile, I definitely recommend going both the hiking and kayaking in Patagonia with Cristian (owner) and his crew. It just doesn't get better than this.

review_text: A few weeks in Chile, and our family recognizes that even public facilities can turn into "tourist trap" destinations. This is a spot that is worth the annoyance of paying for parking, then going through gift store to then pay for entry. Yup, worth it! Park along the road, and if it is extremely crowded, don't go in. Previous reviews have warned that if it is too busy, it isn't enjoyable. The narrow walkways leave people angling for the perfect photo. And what a photo! Really stunning, and noisy, Class VI rapids with Volcan Osorna directly behind, are the visual highlight. The boardwalks are well built, and crowded. Elbow in to take the perfect picture, then head for the less crowded lower trails. We did the one that goes downstream, and it wasn't crowded at all. A lovely side waterfall and private pool that at one time must have been the perfect (but cold) blue lagoon swimming spot, and shaded streamside trail. Two trails totaled 1 kilometer of easy, but not handicap accessible, trail. We skipped the third trail. There are facilities to buy food within the park, and (free) restroom.

review_text: Prior to a recent cruise of South America and Antarctica, we spent four days in Santiago, Chile, where we planned on touring highlights of Santiago and several Chilean wineries. Before our trip, I looked to Trip Advisor for recommendations on top Chilean Tour guides. I was attracted to the excellent reports on “Chilean Wine Lovers” both for wine tours and Santiago City highlights. I contacted the CEO of Chilean Wine Lovers, Maurico Rodriguez and, after a friendly exchange of emails, we planned a tour for each of the four days. My wife and I have done extensive international travel and used some of the highest rated tour agencies in the world. Our experience with Mauricio far exceeded other experiences. Mauricio’s attention to detail and professionalism went far beyond our highest expectations. He arranged for us to be met at the airport, followed by a very informative tour of central Santiago including lunch. On day 2, Mauricio picked us up at the hotel, and 2.5 hours later we arrived at the Aconcagua Valley and visited the Vina San Esteban and Vina Errazuriz Wineries. Both make exceptional wine and Mauricio was a great teacher of the history, soils, climate and production facilities of all wineries visited. Mauricio is truly a wine expert and enjoys sharing his knowledge with his clients. On day 3, Maurico took us to visit the High Maipo Valley, which included stops at the Peres Cruz, Santa Rita Mojaito and Huelqen Wineries. Every day we experienced a fantastic tour, excellent wines, and an enjoyable, fun tour. We ate a great lunch at a restaurant in a rural location only visited by local citizens. The food, ambience and service by the owner were impeccable not to mention the great value. During our stay, Mauricio shared his incredible knowledge of the Chilean Wine Industry with stories, histories, and anecdotes that made each day an adventure as well as a learning experience. Day 4 arrived, and there was Mauricio - waiting to take us to another winery on the way to the port city of Valparaiso. That last wine tour was to the Casablanca Region at Bodega Wines, where they use clay pots for making wine! Each day with Mauricio, we were accompanied by one of his young daughters and on the last day by his two youngest daughters. The girls were truly an added delight to our tours and at the conclusion of our visit, we felt as though we were family! On the way to dropping us at the port in Valparaiso where our cruise ship waited, Mauricio stopped at a convenience store to make a small purchase for us. I joined him in the store and in doing so accidentally dropped my passport on the street while getting out of Mauricio’s van. We proceeded to the port and discovered that my passport was missing. The ship was scheduled to depart in about two hours. Mauricio returned us to the convenience store and talked to the manager. No passport had been turned in to the manager. Mauricio assured us that if the passport had been found by a local resident, it likely would be turned in to the police as local residents know that foreign visitors cannot get out of the country without going to their embassy which would result in their missing the cruise departure. Mauricio then called the police and learned that indeed the passport had been turned in to the police department. Mauricio went to the Police Headquarters, retrieved my passport and took us to the ship in time for departure. All of this was done in the span of 90 minutes in a large port city. We could not have asked for more from Mauricio – he is a wonderful, honest, knowledgeable and well-connected host with a tremendous sense of humor! We feel that we have made a good friend. If you plan to visit Santiago’s wine regions, become knowledgeable of the Chilean Wine Industry, have several great tours, and meet a superb host who will handle all of the details including ensuring your personal safety, contact Mauricio at Chilean Wine Lovers. We will return to Chile in the future -- our first call will be to Mauricio. - JK, Visited December 2015

review_text: The Moneda is the presidential palace in Santiago. It is an imposing, well-maintained building, definitely worth a visit among the key historical sites downtown. Mostly, you can just walk around the building, but there also are interesting exhibits in a subterranean gallery on the Southeast corner of the building. This is the building that was shelled and bombed during the military coup against President Allende in 1973, and from which Allende and his staff fired at tanks from balconies before he committed suicide rather than be taken alive.

review_text: Well, I am a volcano apassionata - I find ways within my budget (and often on the sidelines of a work trip) to get to volcanoes and climb them - the more active, the better. So I have been to volcanoes in Java, Costa Rica, Tanzania, Montserrat, Greece and Italy and loved every one of them. But Villarrica is a thrilling volcano because it's normally covered with snow. That makes it easier to climb (ironically, since you can contour-zigzag) and quicker to get down (since you can toboggan!). Sol y Nieve is a wonderful adventure-sports company in Pucon with seasoned in-house and freelance guides, and a lovely, extremely helpful and bilingual front-desk lady in Bernardita Reyes. At first, one might think that they are a little casual about safety and equipment, but I realized that they are extremely wise, friendly, and sensitive to the mountain, and they don't baby their clients. I loved every moment of this thrilling adventure. Watch it on You Tube or Vimeo (not my videos - Google "climbing volcan Villarrica" or similar) and contact Sol y Nieve. They may not be the cheapest in town, but they have solid credentials and history behind them, and they are far easier for non-Spanish-speaking international clients like me to use. Gracias! Thank you SO much for your wonderful review! We really appreciate the time you have taken to post this write up and are super happy to hear that you had a great and memorable experience with Sol y Nieve! We do hope one day you will return to Pucón to summit Villarrica again and we wish you the best for your next volcano adventure, wherever that may be!

review_text: There is much history with this mountain, looking it up online Charles Darwin climbed it and found new fossils. We hiked Jan 24, 2016. Trail starts near kilometer 70 on route 9. The road was closed at 65km on route 9 with new bridge construction that is closed on weekends. This adds 5 km beach walk to the hike (doubles the distance of hike). We asked a local and heard during the week when the crews are working that the bridge and road are open past this point, but don't count on it. The condition of the new road is very poor past the new bridge and when the crews do allow cars to pass a 4x4 vehicle would be needed if you were allowed to drive all the way to the trailhead. The Tarn trail is overall very visible and easy to follow on a clear day. We found on the way up many orange flags on trees. The trail is cut right through the peatland, and then through the forest, repeating this pattern several times. Once above treeline *about 500m) the trail gets tougher to follow, and was much windier but there are still many flags. There are many trails through muddy pools and even a ravine that was full of snow we had to cross. If you don't have waterproof footwear you will be very wet from this part of the hike. Sometimes I sank in peat and mud up to my knees. There are white poles to follow and more flags on trees in the shrub and peat zone above treeline. To get to the summit peaks and above the shrub-line we needed to climb up about 30-40 meter tall snow slope. Even in January this snow persisted, but was easy to climb up and slide down. Above vegetation line (>650m) there are no markers, and no cairns marking the trail. The slope is loose scree and you need to have sight of the peaks where you are going, or in our case in the middle of an ice storm with low visibility a GPS with the route mapped. You need to be careful near the summits as it is not very clear when you are up there which of them are the real summit. There are a few places with steep crevasse between the hills and on the eastern slopes drops are >100m. After walking over the first large hill or summit, there is the 2nd peak with a trail visibly cut through the scree around the back. This trail leads to the 3rd peak which is the true summit. There is a Chilean flag on the actual summit (photo) that can be visible once you get around the second peak. Do not walk past the Chilean flag, as the drop is vertical and would be deadly. On the way back down it is much easier to get lost, as the flags are somewhat less visible. Most of the way you can follow others tracks. Once back to the beach we needed to hike the 5km back out to the cars again. All together the hike from car to summit to car was about 7 hours.

review_text: Lascar - or Laskar - is 5.600 m above sea level and, even though it's not the hardest climb around San Pedro, the effort you put into it makes reaching the crater a very special experience. It's an easy climb - 800 m up and around 4 km of path -, but you can feel the altitude, therefore you walk pretty slowly. For that reason, it's very important being acclimatised. My boyfriend and I booked the tour with an agency named Ivero, on Caracoles street, and loved it. We were with a group of 7 people and there were 2 guides. One of them spoke reasonable English and they were both very professional. They took our pulse and didn't let us eat much for breakfast, cause digestion takes a lot of oxygen. The price of the tour was 85.0000 pesos per person. It's not cheap, but totally worth it! The agency provides walking poles and boots if you need them. You don't have to be fit to do it, just pay attention if you are feeling headaches or too much dizziness. We had no problem and recommend it! The view from the top and the crater is incredible!

review_text: The funicular Santiago is situated in the Parque Metropolitano. It provides a steep ride from the end of Pio Nono street to the zoo and/or the top of Cerro San Cristobal. It is a very popular attraction, which results in long queues on weekends. Prices also differ depending on the day you visit: they are more expensive on weekends & holidays Adults pay 800 pesos (week) or 1000 pesos (weekend) for a single ride to the zoo; 1500 pesos (week) or 1950 pesos (weekend) for a single ride to or from the top, and 2000 pesos (week) or 2600 pesos (weekend) for a return ride to the top of the hill. My husband is 65+, so he payed 1950 pesos instead of 2600 pesos for a return ride to the top on a Saturday. We had to ask for it in Spanish though, as the price for pensioners wasn't advertised. Winter opening hours are Monday :13- 18 pm., Tuesday-Sunday and holidays : 10 am -19pm Summer opening hours are Monday : 13-20 pm., Tuesday-Sunday and holidays : 10 am-19.45 pm.(last car down) If you want to stop at the zoo you have to do so going up, because the tracks split into two at the zoo station and the car going down doesn't stop there. You can also walk up the (steep) hill to the entrance of the zoo. Be aware that the entire zoo is built on the flanks of the hilll and you have to be fit to climb from one level to the next. There are several benches to rest on along the way, though. ¡Thanks for your opinion! Take Care.

review_text: Magical Day horseback riding and kayaking in Punta Arenas, Chile with Kayak Agua Fresca What a magical day! Claudia was waiting with a sign for us in the parking lot of the port after we cleared security. She was very friendly and spoke good English. She led us to a very nice small bus that we shared with one other family. We drove about 20 minutes to a family farm, where we changed into our kayaking gear, which included pants and a jacket that goes over your clothes. They also gave us water shoes and life jackets. We then drove about 5 minutes to the beach (Strait of Magellan). Johan was our guide and he trained us on the operation of the 2 person kayaks. We kayaked for over an hour down the coast and saw dolphins jumping. Claudia was also kayaking and took family pictures for us (our two children, ages 10 and 13, were with us). After kayaking, we returned to the family farm where we ate a hearty lunch (there was also a vegetarian option). Our kids enjoyed the farm animals, including a lamb, cats and several dogs. Following lunch, the horses were waiting for us just a few steps away and we started the best trail riding experience we have ever had. The horses were calm and well mannered, though my wife said that I got the horse that I deserved (like me, he preferred snacking to walking!). They had 2 guides with the 8 of us, and we didn't just ride around a flat field. Instead, we rode for over two hours and the views were spectacular. Not only did we get to ride through meadows filled with wildflowers, we forded several streams and rivers, traversed a forest and ended up on a mountainside overlooking the Strait. The final trek took us through a stream and then onto the beach for the trip home. One of the horses on the ride had recently foaled and the baby horse (2 months old) followed alongside us on the ride. She was feisty and frisky and so much fun to watch. Every so often, she would kick her back feet in the air and gallop away, then come back close with a toss of her mane. Three of the owner's dogs came along for the walk too and we enjoyed watching them living a dog's best life, free and happy with their paws muddy and their tongues hanging to the ground. We don't know how this day could have been any better. Kudos to Claudia and Kayak Agua Fresca for the experience of a lifetime!

review_text: This winery was included in a tour from Santiago through Chilean Tourist Service. I had not heard of it before (I hadn't done my homework on the wineries of Chile) and I got a real surprise. My tour guide, Javier, had only been at the winery for 4 months but he was very knowledgeable and enthusiastic, and humorous as well! The winery is medium-sized and has been recognised internationally for its consistency and innovative single terroir wine styles. The short tour of the vineyard was very instructive - a plot of labelled vines of different types and a small underground viewing area so you can see the layers of the soil in which the vines are growing, including how far down the roots go. The tasting consisted of 4 wines - "Pomerape" 2012, a very nice sauvignon blanc only available at the winery, "Sibaris" 2012 carmenere, a red grape variety now only found in Chile (it died out in the Medoc in the late 19th century phylloxera outbreak) with a very nice nose and flavour, "Founder's Collection" 2009 cabernet sauvignon, which was sensational, and a late-harvest Semillon/chardonnay, which was very pleasant. You get to keep the wine tasting glass. Another aspect of the visit, which I did not expect at all, was the "museum quality" of a display of ancient and historic artefacts relating to the Mapuche indigenous people. I say museum quality not only for the actual items on display but for the way they are displayed. One of the owners has a special interest in supporting these people through the educational aspects of the displays, in and around the buildings - the landscaped gardens are small but beautiful and include wooden totem sculptures - but especially through donating money to the community from the sale of wine with their "Aliwen" label. The American wine magazine "Wine & Spirit" just voted Underraga "Winery of the Year", and I can see why. Don't miss it if you're visiting Santiago.

review_text: This tour starts early. Our guide pick us up around 5:30am. It took 1.5 hour to arrive the geyser field so we are there around 7am. When we went was January and the weather is not as cold as we thought. This place is located in high altitude (4320 meters) so it's best to visit geyser after you stay in town for couple days. Couple people on our tour couldn't enjoy the hot sprint because they are not feeling well due to the high altitude. There are many geysers (>80) so it's a pleasure to walk around in the field and enjoy the scenery. After that, we can go to the hot spring in the geyser field for about an hour. He hot spring has only one section that is hot so most people are hanging out there. After the hot spring, the tour takes us to the wet land where we can see many desert animals (flamingos, birds, vicuña , llama ... Etc). Very nice and beautiful. In the village we also tried the llama skillet and that is very tasty. (A lot better than the llama we tried in the restaurant). Recommend to take a small size tour so you don't have to wake up at 4am to wait for the pick up. Our tour pick up time is 5 to 5:30am.

review_text: On my first ever visit to Santiago de Chile, I contacted Kylie to ask if she would be able to do a relaxed gourmet wine visit and lunch near Santiago. I had been traveling for 6 weeks on long distance buses from Buenos Aires to Patagonia and then back up to Santiago. I wanted a low-key lunch that would out of, but within an hour, of the city. Most importantly, I wanted to treat myself to some great Chileno food and wine! Kylie had a small lunch tour going to a gorgeous winery called Casas del Bosque about 1 hour west of Santiago de Chile (on the road to Valparaiso). Kylie took us there for a bit of wine tasting and a scrumptious 5-course lunch. Immediately the waiter arrived at our table with a lovely freshly cooked bread and the ubiquitous Chilena salsa of pebre, along with a lovely glass of Sauvignon Blanc. Many of the courses were served with some of the top wines that this bodega produces, including a delicious Sauvignon Blanc and Pinot. The wine and food pairings were fantastic. I thoroughly enjoyed every lip-smacking course... and every wine that went with it. At the end of the meal, I for one didn't really want to go on the scheduled wine tour, opting instead to sit on the lovely couches in the tranquil garden at the winery and have another class of their Gran Reserva Pinot. Kylie quickly reorganised with the winery and I had another leisurely hour in the garden before we headed back to Santiago. Kylie did a fabulous job organising a perfect day out - easy travel distance, delicious food and wine in a very low key and tranquil setting, away from the hustle-bustle of the city. I give Kylie 5 stars for great personalised service. She delivered a tour that had everything that I wanted... and more. I will definitely do another tour with Kylie when I am next back in Santiago! Thanks for your review. I know your tour was a while ago, and I'm so glad that it was still fresh in your mind by the time we were listed here on TripAdvisor. And with great photos too! I hope to see you if you're back in Chile sometime soon. Best wishes!

review_text: I loved the rambling layout of Neruda's home in Santiago and seeing how he and Matilde lived. The home is decorated in simple, artsy and quirky style and very much a reflection of a creative mind. It's too bad photography isn't allowed as I would love to have had some graphic reminders to have at home. Not sure why it's such a taboo - there really isn't anything there that's that unusual or priceless. Heck, the Louvre lets you take photos! I was, however, a little dismayed to see all the ivy covering one of the outside walls of the home. That is not beneficial to a historic home in any regard and looks as if that ivy's been growing there a while. And since the foundation charges a rather high entry fee in benefit to the home, I hope they would use part of that for the home's upkeep. Overall, it's a short tour, pleasant and not mentally taxing. We enjoyed spending Saturday morning there.

review_text: This trip was something i havent done before in my life so it was exciting to me. People said if you did something similar before, you wouldnt find this amusing. Anyway, the tour bus came slightly later than they said they would but it was alright. The tour guide, Jorge, a thin man with curly hair, was very friendly and funny. He managed to explain everything very well switching between English and Spanish. He also let us know when you should use the toilets as there will not be any toilets from which point to which point. Before the island was a journey across the deserts, we managed to see some wildlife, cactus, deers and foxes. It was a fun thing to see. The tour towards the island with animals was great! Especially the part where the boat was moving and chasing the dolphins! It was very entertaining and eventhough it was cold, the excitement warmed all of us up! We also got to see sea lions laying lazily on the rocks, different types of birds and what they do or how to distinguish them (thanks to our knowledgeable tour guide) and penguins too! However, the penguins were a disappointment because there were only a few of them >< the tour guide said theres a season where the penguins will bring their hatchlings down and swim. Sadly the end of October wasnt the season =( anyway, we got compensated with the sightings of sea otters! The tour guide said it was a rare scene, dont know how true is that but it was fun to look at =) After the animals, we disembarked at another island where we were given an hour to explore the island. 1 hour wasnt enough to explore the entire island if you are walking around slowly and taking pictures along the way. I decided to hike up the hill to get a view of the entire island and the sea, it took me 40mins to go up, snap lots of pictures, and come back down. After that, we headed back for lunch at about 3.30pm, lunch arrived about 4pm. The portion was small, not enough for a big eater like me but the food was good. Overall a good experience! Would definitely recommend it! But i would recommend it on seasons where the penguins are with their hatchlings at the bottom of the hills, definitely not end of october.

review_text: Going to a cemetery on vacation sounds kind of odd, but its really amazing. Take the subway to the cemetery stop and wander down to the oldest crypts. The architectural styles vary from gothic revival to neoclassical to art deco and are all unique and interesting. Several presidents are buried here as well as other cultural leaders of Chile. The cemetery remains active and you may see a funeral. Near the main gate (which is on the opposite side of the cemetery from where you enter if you come off the subway) and in the square outside it were large displays about the different groups that settled Chile. It was quiet, restful, and interesting. I think I took more pictures here than anywhere else on our trip.

review_text: The trip through the fjords is fantastic with magical landscapes all the way up until the end. Snowy, rocky, forested and steamy mountains, waterfalls, volcanoes, narrow passes… in all sorts of lightning (sunrise, sunset, at night, misty, etc.). Do not forget to look at the stars, as if the night is clear you may get to see the Milky Way, the Southern Cross and the Magellan Clouds, among others. Besides, the staff at the ship were very friendly and willing to help. Food was also good. Catching up with fellow travelers from around the world and with truck drivers from Chile was also a highlight. We were two wheelchair users, but we could not stay at the wheelchair accessible room because there was only one low bed. We stayed at a regular cabin and occupied the two lower bunk beds and NaviMag left free the accessible cabin, so that we could use the bathroom and shower. Even though, boarding and disembarking was a bit difficult with the wheelchairs (the ramp to get to the ship is steep and has anti-slipping metal bands for cars and trucks not to slip in bad weather), we could move quite freely between decks 5 and 6 (passenger decks). Some of the doors to the decks had a lower step (about 2 inches) that was easier to overcome (others were about 6 inches) and there was always someone to help if doors were shut (they are all very heavy, including cabin doors). Thus, if you can get over 2 inch steps, you should be alright. The only inconvenience was our ferry leaving a couple of days later than scheduled, so do not plan anything important the days after the expected arrival and have some flexibility of schedule if you plan on taking the ship. That we would depart one day later we knew 15 days in advance, but the extra delayed day was adjourned on the same night that we had to board due to bad weather, so we had to find accessible accommodation in a rush, which was not easy, as our previous hotel was full for the night. All in all, we feel that communication could have been clearer, but that is the only downside of the whole experience. We would also like to give special thanks to Gaspar, Camila, Alexia and all the crew for helping us throughout the whole trip. During meals, they helped us carry the trays and they were always attentive to our needs. They also arranged that the van that picked us up could enter the port and come near the ship. So all in all great service from the NaviMag team. If you are not tight on schedule and want to wind down a bit and do some slow tourism, this is your trip.

review_text: A well traveled friend once told me one should never have favourites when travelling, after visiting Torres Del Paine National Park I find it extremely hard not to... We visited just as the first snows had arrived in April 2015. The scenery is absolutely stunning and the various hikes that one can go on will fulfill anyone's "into the wild" desires. We visited the Mirador Torres, Valle de Frances, Los Cuernos, Lago Pehoé Paine Grande and Lago Skóttsberg (sort of a revised take on the popular "W" hike). All were stunning but if I were pushed for time I'd recommend the Torres and the boat trip across the Lago Pehoé. There's plenty more to see and you probably wouldn't run out of new sights if you spent 10 days or more here. We unfortunately only had 4 days so we might just have to do a return journey sometime in the future. Liked Most: Incredible awe inspiring scenery. Liked Least: Quite an undertaking just to get to the park (that could of course be a positive in many a travelers book though).

review_text: We started in San Pedro de Atacama. We purchased the tour 2 days before. The office hours are not exactly the same as shown here on tripadvisor... Seems they take a siesta during the day. We purchased the private room also on the first day for extra. The transfer from Chilean minivan to Bolivian 4x4 went smoothly, although there were no toilets at either border. When we signed up, they told us they already have filled up one car and in the second car there was only one couple and us if we signed up. When we were transfered to the 4x4, we were put in a car with 6 people total, not 4. We tried to figure out why it was done like this, due to private accomadation, etc, but couldn't come up with logical answer. So if they tell you at the office that there are only 4 people in car so far fpr second group, doesn't mean you will be in this car. It is little cramped with 6 people in one car, but it is doable. You switch the seating each day, but we found to be the furthest back seat for two most comfortable. If you are less then 180cm tall, then you should be fine, don't expect lot of leg room but you have lot of room on the side which is nice for backpack etc. All other seats, you had to have the backpack on your lap or between legs. The accomadations were actually quite better, then we expected, especially the first day, we even had our private shower. They have solar heating so need to take quick showers, which is fine. It was quite simple accomadation. The food was actually good, but be sure to ask if they serve lama if you don't want to eat it. In Bolivia, the time changes so make sure you have correct time so you do not wait for dinner one hour thinking they are late or wake up one hour too early for breakfast... The locals gave us looks, as to why are they awake already. The high elevation is felt, but if you stay few days at San Pedro and do some day trips, you should be fine. Coca leaves helped as well. Andreas, our tour guide, was very good amd funny. Even though they promised us that guide will speak about 30% english, he spoke about 5-10% english. The other guide spoke better english. But he explained to us things as well, and we tried to understand with our basic spanish and his basic english, in the end it was fine. His driving was quite good and safe. He even took us on a top of a rock, where we had to do little climbing, which other tours seems did not do. The view was nice. At the salt flats, his proximity picture taking skills were not as good as other drivers had, when we saw pictures of some other groups. It took a while for our group to get a hang of it, it is not as easy as it seems. The food Andreas prepared was excellent. The car had trouble only once, due to engine overheating, but Andreas fixed it after while. I am not surprised that the car overheated, due to high altitude and terrain, and they only put water in the radiator, and not a mixture of anti-freeze, which has much higher boiling temp. Maybe it would be time to change the refrigerant in the A/C as the air was not that cold. Otherwise our tour was overall very nice experience.

review_text: This was an incredible experience all around. If you're looking to learn a lot about astronomy and see some incredible constellations and celestial bodies look no further. First Jorge picks you up at your hotel and takes you to his private stargazing property far away from any light pollution. You are given a warm poncho/blanket and seat and then start the experience with a lecture from Jorge about various topics such as how a telescope works, history of astronomy and he points out various constellations and celestial bodies that you can see with the naked eye. Afterwards you take a break where food and drinks will be provided and you all sit around a warm fire (which is very nice on a cold desert night). Honestly we were impressed with the spread of food (light bites, pastries and snacks) and drinks (both alcoholic and non-alcoholic) that were provided. Finally, you start viewing various celestial bodies through the telescopes. Because of the wide range of telescopes Jorge has, you get to see various objects at various distances which all look incredible. Jorge is an incredibly knowledgeable astronomer and was able to answer any question we had whether it be about the history of an object or the science behind it. We really can't recommend this experience enough, if you're interested in a stargazing tour look no further than Atacama Desert Stargazing!

review_text: Staying at Hotel Las Torres this park was the experience of a lifetime. It was declared a world biosphere reserve in 1978. I arrived late in the afternoon to see hundreds of guacanos running down the hill to cross the road in front of us and head up the other side. It's puma country and apparently they can come close to the hotel around March. I went on a 6km hike and at the summit (it's not that hard) a condor flew overhead as if to check us out. My guide said 'This is the real Patagonia' but I was choked up and couldn't answer. The tours and walks are extensive and varied to suit anyone's level of fitness and the guides are smart, patient, knowledgeable and all pretty easy to converse with. I went at the beginning of the season which can see 250,000 visitors, as I'd rather a cold day than hordes of people, but then it's only the lucky few in the world who see this park in their lifetime. The rest of my trip included the Pantanal (Pantanal Jaguar Safaris, contact Leen) and the Stella Australis which makes the next holiday hard to top.

review_text: In May of this year my daughter and I visited Patagonia. We stayed in Puerto Natales. We went with Angelo and Niko to Lago Grey to kayak. I have to say this was one of the best days I have ever had. We got an early start and saw the countryside of Patagonia at sunrise. It was absolutely beautiful. We stopped numerous times on the way to the park to take pictures of the various sights along the way. Angelo seemed as excited about this as we were, taking pictures of his own. We got to Lago Grey. Angelo had everything we needed to go kayaking: the boats, the gear, the protective clothing, everything. We had a brief tutorial about kayaking safety and off we went. What we saw then was like nothing I have ever seen in person. Shortly we were up upon some of the most beautiful icebergs that have come off Glacier Grey at the other end of the lake. We felt like little kids. The wonder of the place is hard to describe. I felt like I was in a National Geographic photo shoot. You could tell that Angelo and Niko also appreciated the experience also. They were the guides, of course, but they seemed more like our good friends who took us to their favorite place. We had lunch on a rock cliff. Angelo brought plenty of everything for some hungry kayakers. They took our cameras at the beginning of the trip and shot great pictures and videos throughout the trip. The pace was our own and totally unhurried. It is a an experience my daughter and I will never forget. I wish everyone could have a day like this. It was largely the location and the sights but also due to the great way Angelo took care of all the details and just let us immerse ourselves in the experience. I can highly recommend this for a once in a lifetime experience. Thanks again Angelo and Espiritu Patagon. Tom and Hali

review_text: I just completed the roundtrip Puerto Montt-Puerto Natales-Puerto Montt on the Eden at the end of June 2015. The observations of other travelers remain relevant, but some things are new. Although the ferry had only a handful of passengers (except for the Puerto Eden- Puerto Natales stretch where it provides local transportation) there was no interaction with the deck officers and the bridge remained off-limits at all times. Panoramic views of the waterworld were available only from the open decks on a ferry steaming through snow and ice. Summer side trips to a glacier and a visit if Puerto Eden are no longer offered. There is television on board, but only soccer games and hype were on. Smoking is allowed and done only outside. A fixed course meal is served at set hours in the cafeteria. The food is tasty and ample enough. Between meals fruit juice is available, but no soft drinks or snacks can be bought. Alcohol is no longer allowed on board (supposedly some drunk truckers were barbequeing in their cabin and set the ship on fire, although they just may have tried to stay warm). The local passengers provide for themselves and carry on what they need. Of special importance is the fact that the frerry schedule is only approximate. For example, the schedule of my northbound leg had a listed Tuesday departure and Thursday morning arrival. The ferry arrived late in Puerto Natales, so the return trip left on Saturday and arrived on Tuesday afternoon. Reasons for delays are loading problems, high winds and the need to pass tricky passages in daylight with the proper stage of the tide.The ferry can only be late, but never be early, and it generally cannot make up delays. Navimag appears to offer full refunds if a trip must be called off because of delays, but travellers with non-refundable air tickets better have cancellation insurance in case of late arrival (make sure that high winds and contrary tides are not considered excludable acts of God). Added attractions are a possibly very choppy 18 hour stretch of open ocean and, on a northbound leg, the opportunity to share the boat with truck trailers full of cattle on their way to slaughter. And always, the bunks come with bedding, but towels are not provided. For a rare but extreme Navimag adventure google the "wreck of the Navimag Amadeo". Enjoy the trip! I did - both ways (cattle or not)! The fact that Chile won the Copa Americana 2015 helped.
