review_text: My partner and I went on this tour and it included 5 others in our direct group. It was a really fun day!I have a few recommendations for those booking this tour: (1) wear closed toe, comfortable sneakers as you will be walking the grounds of wineries and there may be some mud, (2) the tour companies communicate via WhatsApp and it works really well in case you want to download this app before arriving in Santiago (3) eat breakfast and hydrate before the tour, lunch was around 2 for us. It is a long day and there are excellent wines to indulge in on this tour. We booked our tour about a month in advance and received a confirmation pretty quickly afterward. Our scheduled tour was on a Monday and received a WhatsApp message for hotel pick up time about 12 hours before the start of tour, Sunday at around 8 PM local time in Santiago. This practice seems normal for the tours here, so do not fret if you haven't received a pick up notification until the night before your tour. Our pick up was right on time. Benjamin was our guide and he made the day very enjoyable, and our driver was Ricardo who delivered us safely throughout the day. Our first stop was a modern winery with a beautiful building and well manicured landscape, Vinedos Veramonte. The wine tasting featured 4 wines. None of these wines really spoke to us. We spent some time walking the grounds here and they were very beautiful. Also, got to see some alpacas. Then, we went to Casa Villa Vinamar that included all sparkling wines that were delicious. We enjoyed the grounds here which looked like a palace with a large fountain in the front. Next, we went to Bodegas RE winery, our favorite of the day. The wines here were all very special. They utilize Carignon in some of their blends and have a stand alone with that grape, which is rare. This was our favorite wine in all of the tastings in Chile. Lastly, we got lunch at the Vina Casas del Bosque winery that featured dishes paired with their wine. All food and wine here was delicious. This tour was such a fun way to experience the Chilean countryside, and drink delicious wines. Review of: Exclusive wineries in Casablanca Valley & Tanino Restaurant

We went out on a Monday when most wineries were closed but Nick used his connects to open up 5 outstanding locations for us. Here are my thoughts on 3 of them. Our first stop was at the Viña Antiyal where we learned all about Biodynamic Garagiste wine production. Don’t know much about Biodynamic Garagiste? You will when you leave! The rooftop patio we did our tasting on overlooked acres of grapevines and the Andes mountains in the background. It was then off to the Perez Cruz vineyard for a look at a larger production boutique winery. Their main facility was designed by renowned architect José Cruz Ovalle and it’s enchanting! The wine isn’t so bad either ;) Each tasting is paired with a local cheese, nut or chocolate. And make sure they pour you a glass of their rosé. Our day wrapped up with a quick trip to the William Fèvre winery. Here is where got to try Victor Pino Torche‘a award winning Espino Reserva Especial Chardonnay. I wanted to buy a case and bring it back with me! Needless to say, when we were dropped back off at our hotel we were happy, filled with knowledge and more than a little tipsy. Enjoy the trip! Review of: Full-Day Wine Tour from Santiago with Sommelier Guide

review_text: We traveled here as a family of 4 adults. We hiked only 1 portion, the west leg of the W from Refugio Grey to Refugio Paine Grande. On the map, it shows 11km and estimated 3 hours. However, we took 5 hours to complete the hike. The first half is mostly uphill, and the second half is mostly downhill. We hiked on a very windy day; our kayaking excursion earlier in the day was cancelled due to the wind. We visited in late December, and the temperature was around 50 degrees F but with variable, strong winds and rain. Waterproof jacket and pants are recommended. The trail is well-maintained and clearly marked. We originally intended to hike more on the following days, however we are around 60yrs old and not regularly active, so we decided this was all we could handle for now. Our adult children did hike from Refugio Paine Grande towards Camp Italiano on the second day. This is a beautiful trail to hike, however you have to come prepared. Be aware that it is harder to hike with packs, and hiking sticks were a huge plus for us.

review_text: Much of the Atacama is just the poor man's version of Bolivia—except at 10 times the price! Laguna Chaxa is the perfect example of what I'm talking about: the flamingo lagoons and salt flats here utterly pale in comparison to their counterparts in Bolivia, which are just a few hours away by car. Yes, Bolivia is higher altitude and requires more acclimatizing, but it's so worth the effort. If you're coming all the way to the Atacama to see flamingos and salt flats, please do yourself a favor and add Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni and Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve to your itinerary. They're much cheaper, less crowded, and far more spectacular than what this place offers.

If you're coming all the way to the Atacama to see flamingos and salt flats, please do yourself a favor and add Bolivia's Salar de Uyuni and Eduardo Avaroa National Reserve to your itinerary. They're much cheaper, less crowded, and far more spectacular than what this place offers.

review_text: The attention given to tourists is terrible! On 06/9 it was raining and most of the trips were outside and they did not offer umbrellas. What could have been an unpleasant but excusable mistake became worse when at the beginning of the tour I complained to the guide Marta, who was wearing an umbrella and didn't even offer her umbrella or apologize, but kept trying to explain why we should accept getting wet! When I told him that if there was no solution, he just had to apologize, he said he wouldn't apologize! Rude! Who is the manager that allows such a person to serve customers? When the Tasting began, the first three wines were presented in an external area with people standing in front of a counter. The wines were reasonable. The second part presented by sommelier Teo was adequate, in a comfortable room and accompanied by cheese, but it did not have the main wine: Don Merchor Cabernet Sauvignon. Opposite the exit from the Tasting room was the Restaurant but to gain access, despite having a closed door, we were forced to walk all the way around the outside area in the rain, the same route to go to the bathroom. We went for lunch: we ordered a salad to share and two pastas. The salad didn't come first but with the pasta which was cold and I had to ask for it to be warmed up. I asked for a glass of Terráyuno wine to go with it, and to my surprise they didn't present the bottle, the label, much less the taste: it came with a glass served with less than a portion in my opinion. The seafood pasta had a hospital taste: no taste of anything, just pepper that we asked for and added. I thought it was better not to risk even the coffee, I paid the bill without the services and I will never go back! The wifi requires a password from the bracelet and drops out all the time and needs to be restarted, meaning they don't even offer this quality. For a long time now, this winery has lived more on tradition than on its products. Casilero is a bad wine, but cheap. The best are more expensive than they deserve, made on an industrial scale and do not have a good cost-benefit ratio. We came from Mendoza where we were wonderfully treated in all the wineries, from the biggest like Monteviejo to the small ones like Masi Tupungato, any of them infinitely better and more attentive. At no point, whether the guide or Somelier asked for our assessment, it doesn't seem to matter. Who knows, I'll read it here, but I doubt it will have any effect. I do not recommend! Outra recomendaçao que podemos fazer para vc, é verificar o estado do clima antes de comprar um passeio, assim vc fica no hotel sim molhar.

review_text: This is quite a unique spot, located at 4'200 meters altitude, where you can explore the geysirs and hot ponds on your own. Very little people, as a matter of fact, we were only the two of us ... :-) Easy to find: Set your navi to Mauque, coming either from Colchane or Huara, driving on the A-15. Then turn on to the A-487, heading for Mauque. From there, you will see sign-posts and the location is really easy to find. Google Maps lists it as "Campo geotérmico de Puchuldiza". The A-487 is a dirt road, but a very soft one. No bumps, no holes. Only two very tiny creek crossings, one 50cm wide and the other 2 meters wide; both approx. 20cm deep. No problem even for a 2WD car; maybe a little more height, e.g. with a cross-over can help, but not mandatory. The Geysirs spout continuously, since some years ago a geothermal company explored the area, and plugged some pipes into the ground. Before, the geysirs were spouting every so often, like the ones in Iceland, but now there is a continous flow of hot water being shot in thte air by several Geysirs; we had three "running" at the same time. Plus many water and mud pools. On top of this, there is - of course - the beautifully coloured valley with all the sulfur minerals giving great many colours. Finally, there is also a hot water pool - with changing rooms male/female ! All of the area is very clea, and the car tracks are marked with red stones, so that the thermal features are preserved. If everyone sticks to being careful with these hot springs, they will remain super-beautiful for many years ahead, and provide tavellers with a superb one-of-its-kind experience !

review_text: This is one of the more rougher treks I've done. Both in terms of adressing my routefinding skills many times (while there is a collection of signposting as well as the much more frequent markerstones, I did manage to wander off track quite a few times) as in the actual difficulty of the terrain (boulder hopping, steep descents, muddy marshes, negotiating tree roots & branches) your progress will be slow each of the 3 or more days you're trekking the 32km/20mi long Dientes. I solo-hiked it in 4. But they say: the rougher the trek, the more beautiful it gets. That counts here also. It's a little more wilderness than the one in Torres del Paine. While you're on the most southerly inhabited island of the world in Puerto Williams, a Chilean Armada town slowly growing into a tourist destination, enjoy the view of Cerro Bandera while you start your climb. On top there's a beautiful view of the Beagle Channel and Argentina's Tierra del Fuego mountains across. Continue along the edges of the ridge to a steep drop to Laguna del Salto, one of the many tundra lakes in the area. I stayed here for the night on a terribly wet and uneven floor, but with fresh water. My second day started with a climb up to Paso Australia and over loose boulders up Paso los Dientes (I wandered off track here which did cost me half an hour) to eventually descent to Laguna los Dientes and Laguna Escondida again with plenty big boulders to hop. Campsites and water were no problem finding here and were in better condition. There's a beautiful view of the jagged peaks of the actual Dientes ('teeth' in spanish), for which the area is named. On a clear day the more southerly Lago Windhond is visible as are the Cabo de Hornos islands. My third day ended up being the easiest one. Only two easier uphill sections and drops to arrive at the beaver affected area of big Laguna Martillo, where I took a wrong direction again costing me about 45 minutes. After the big lake there's a beautiful valley to cross where I saw signs of a big animal nearby, possibly a puma. I eventually camped at the foot of the biggest climb of the whole trek, Paso Virginia. The fourth day started with a muddy ascent of the lower section of the climb and ended at a fantastic overview of a very steep and possibly dangerous descent to Laguna Guanacos. Take care here in bad weather. After this lake there is a long mixed section of marshes, woods and farmland to get you down to the end of the trail at an old fishery at the road which will lead you to Puerto Williams again in 2 hours. I only saw people on the first night and was thus almost the whole time alone on the trail. Weather can be a problem here because of the southerly location of the Island, but most of the time I was hiking in clear sunny skies in late March 2017. Recommended.

review_text: We booked a guided trip to summit volcan villarica with this company. The main reason for doing this was because We were arriving in late to pucon the night before summiting (only one good day weather was forecast for the next day) and we because of this we could not rent the required equipment to summit on time (crampons, ice axe, helmet etc). This is a really easy hike if you have some experience with mountains and you can definetly do this without a guide if you have time to organise renting equipment. However the company were really nice from the very start. They stayed open late (over an hour and a half late) to fit us with our gear on the night before summiting. The next morning picked us up from our hostel and brought us to the mountain in a pickup. We were in a small group of 6 which we then split into two groups along the way due to different fitness levels. Three of us went ahead with one guide at a faster pace to the others. I really appreciated this as up to that point I had been frustrated by the slow pace of the group. The guides were all really cool and full of good conversation (in english). We enjoyed a long break at the top and returned by sledding down the snowy part of the mountain before reaching the scree and walking the rest of the way. We then returned to pucon where we shared some beers on the roof of their shop. Overall this was a really good experience which I would 100% recommend if you have NO mountain experience. If you have some experience I would recommend renting equipment and doing it by yourself. wow we feel praised with such a wide comment, thanks for the time for sharing your experience. review_text: If you are interested in going to Patagonia, I strongly recommend booking with Extremo Chile. My friend and I booked a 3 night, 4 day guided W trek experience of Torres Del Paine and it was incredible. Not only was the trek and the landscape picturesque but having a guided tour and everything organised for us made it even more worthwhile and enjoyable. A few call-outs that made our experience amazing and why you should book with Extremo Chile if you’re considering going to Torres Del Paine: 1. Communication prior to the trip was excellent. Carlos (the owner of Extremo Chile) replied quickly to all our questions and provided us with a packing list of things to take on our trip. 2. Carlos came to our hotel the day before the hike to confirm we had everything we needed and to answer any other questions we had. When we looked at other companies offering tours of the W trek - they included this as part of the first day to make it seem like a longer trek but you only need to do the W trek in 3 nights / 4 days. Carlos also picked us up from the hotel the morning of the first day. 3. The food was exceptional!!!!! And there was plenty of it, which you need especially walking so much. Carlos cooked for us each night and we had great fresh food. Carlos made sure to also cater for our dietary requirements. We also even had wine and beer some nights with our food! 4. The service was amazing. We booked the camping W trek, and each night when we arrived at the campsites, our tents were already set up for us and the tent, mats and sleeping bags were premium quality. We also didn’t have to carry any of these which was amazing, we only carried our snacks and personal items for the hike each day. Carlos also let us borrow hiking poles for the duration of the hike and lent us ice crampons for the first day as the Towers were quite icy. He also lent us water proof bags to put some of our clothes in when it rained one day. 5. The guide was incredible and so knowledgeable. He had 20+ years experience of Patagonia and we were able to appreciate the walk so much more. 6. It is such great value for money in comparison to other companies we were looking at. Even if you choose to not get a guide, I would still recommend the unguided tour at Extremo Chile as the food and the hire equipment at the Campsites each night (if available) are so expensive. I wish I could give more than 5 stars. I have recommended to all my friends and family! If you are going to Patagonia, you must book with Extremo Chile.

review_text: We had heard that the Sky Constanera was expensive and just another observation deck. I’m so glad we decided to go and didn’t listen to that! Yes, it does cost money to go up but it is worth it. We went up on a Saturday afternoon around 1pm and had the place basically entirely to ourselves. There were probably 5-10 other people around. The views are stunning and there are plaques explaining what you are looking at as well as small speakers you can hear describing what you are viewing when you stand right under them. There are two levels that you get access to when you pay to go up. The highest level is literally the highest level. When you look up, it’s open air!! To me that was so cool because most observation decks don’t have that feature. You can read about the construction of the building and there is a chart showing how it compares to other tall buildings around the world. We really enjoyed our time here and spent about 45 minutes really enjoying it. When you enter you go through a meta detector and your bag is x-rayed. After that, you have a brief wait and while the elevator goes up the guide in the elevator explained in English and Spanish a bit about the building. When you’re ready to head down, there is an area to line up and the guide in the elevator heading down was very friendly and chatted with us about how we enjoyed the experience. We were shocked at how we didn’t have to wait more than a minute and there were no lines. He said we were there during lunch time and that helped reduce the amount of people who would normally be there. It is a little confusing when you enter the mall to figure out how to go to the look out. Go to one of the white electronic guides. It basically looks like a giant iPad or computer screen on a holder. You can change the language to English if need be and it will tell you exactly where to go from where you are to access the entry to the look out. All in all, totally worth it. Definitely a must do while in Santiago!

review_text: I put below review here not to scare everyone, but I do want to hi light some facts about the hike. when the accident happened on the1st of March causing 2 death, several injuries, my boyfriend and I were just there. Although with another tour operator, we still find the whole tour needs add more security meaturement. Luckily with only 5 people in the team, the situation was a lot easier to control. we were still going up when the weather condition changed dramatically. certain points we couldn't see much, only wind and snow blowing to our face, and freezing. It was bad. I was so scared that I called it off when we literally 20 meters away from the top, I insisted to one of guide to go down. so 3 others continued with an older guide, me and my boyfriend turn back. Now i think about it, I was so happy that I made that choice. There is no meaning to risk your life just to see nothing! The only thing to use to hold yourself is a ice axe. If you have never used such thing before, don't expect you can stop yourself sliding by using the little tool. about 2300 meters when we add ice spikes to our shoes, the guides used 1 mins to explain what to do if you fall. To me this is ridiculous!! If nothing happens, great! BUT if something happens, just like the 2 death happened on that day, you can't expect yourself react so fast! From all the blogs, post and travel books we read, the only thing mentioned about the hike is Physically fit, honestly I think there are a lot more than that. these 2 death were 20 years old young boys, I bet yes they were! Accidents happen of course, maybe it was the terribly bad weather on that day, or maybe it was the careless, but overall I think the security of the operators all have issues. It's not a W-tour or a hike to the lake. I want to share my opinion sincerely with you, and I hope people read this review knowing what they expect from the hike.

review_text: Being quite disorganised I hadn't planned ahead to be able to do the W or the O but I still made it to the Torres on a one-day hike. Buses leave early, and at the same times irrespective of the company, from the main bus station in Puerto Natales, and the ticket is a return one. Shop around - most are priced at 15,000 return, I got mine for 12,000. The bus journey takes about 90 minutes. When you arrive you need to queue for park entrance - be sure to get the back of your ticket stamped if you are there for the day but plan to return, as the ticket is valid for 3 days, but only if stamped. Then it's an extra 3000 pesos for the return coach to the start of the trail up to the Torres. Here you will also find a cafe and a Patagonia store. It took me 3h20 to reach the Mirador Las Torres. There is a path but it is rough in places and most importantly, it is very undulating, so don't expect to save any time on the way back. It is also a scramble over a very rocky part to reach the mirador - just when you think you're nearly there, you have to content within a very rocky stretch - a scramble and then a climb up. The views are rather stunning the whole way, and if you're lucky you'll get to see the helicopter ferrying goods in and litter out. There is a cafe and toilets about half way. It's an intense walk - I had planned to return to the park the day after but was too tired and aching. But it was completely worth it, and I can't wait to go back and do the O! Be sure to make it back to the cafe at the start of the trail for the last connecting bus to the park entrance! It's unlikely you'll want to walk the extra kms!

Tip: take a community taxi from the local township. They run pass the site every 10 minutes and are ultra cheap.

review_text: We were warned repeatedly that the early morning trips to the Geysers were very cold and to dress warm, but the long and freezing cold bus ride there was one of the most miserable travel experiences I've had. (Of course, that could be unique to our tour company.) In any case, the geysers were interesting, but not enough to justify the journey and discomfort. And I'm not a wimpy US snob tourist... I love backpacking and have slept in snow caves on various trips. The thing that killed us was that the thermal spring you can swim in was supposed to be a highlight, and instead it barely felt warmer than the air. Maybe it was an unusual day, but our guide said people claim it's 35 degrees (C) but is really more like 30. It cannot possibly have been more than 25 when we got it. As soon as I was in, I wanted to get out, I was no more comfortable inside than out. Fortunately, the amazing views of the beautiful mountains all around and the cool places we stopped on the way back to San Pedro after the frigid and disappointing morning made the whole ordeal worth it. But my advice is make sure your tour company has a comfortable and heated bus to get you there, and DO NOT get in to the spring unless you feel it with your hand first and are confident you will not regret it.

review_text: Maybe all the other tourists had had a big night the night before, or maybe it was because it was a day for going to the beach, but at 9am I was the only one wanting to go on the walking tour of the city. Thankfully the guide, Felipe, was more than happy to give a tour just for me. I say just for me, that would be forgetting the pack of stray dogs that followed the tour route with us (they're completely harmless, though they test their luck chasing passing cars). Felipe was a great guy and an informative guide, tailoring the information he gave to keep it interesting for someone my age with lots of anecdotes and local legends. He also didn't just talk about Valpo, answering my questions about student life and politics in Chile (there was a public sector strike in Valpo, so no funiculars or museums were open). Afterwards he translated for me at the pharmacy to help me get some medicine which worked, so that was much appreciated too! Definitively a worthwhile half-day and introduction to a chaotic but interesting place.

review_text: The lagoons were paired with our visit to the flamingo reserve and what a treat it was to have those two sites in the same tour. After seeing the wonders of the flamingoes, we really didn't anticipate doing more than enjoying the sight of the ultramarine blue water and scruffy terrain and flora, with volcanoes as backdrop. But the vicunas had something else in mind entirely, much to our delight. As we stood watching a lone flamingo feeding at the edge of the second lagoon, and our guide pointed out some nesting Chilean geese, two bands of vicuna (each male has a harem of about a dozen females plus their young) sauntered down the hill to a salt lick adjacent to the water and converged at the base of the hill. Because males are very competitive, there was some posturing from the two leading their respective families. As they did their thing, the females and young darted around, clearly happy to interact with newcomers. They pranced back and forth together along the edge of the lagoon. Young vicuna chased each other while one or two females kept an eye to make sure they didn't wander too far. It was like "a ballet being born out in the valley" (sorry Bruce!) right before our very eyes. And once the males had sorted out their differences, the vicunas formed a single file and walked along the laguna, sometimes into it, and then headed toward the other laguna. Our guide was as delighted as we were. He had never seen anything like it. The scene made for a most memorable visit!

The staff were so lovely and we had a delicious dinner. The second night we stayed at a Salt Hotel owned by the company and it was spotless. Hot water, wifi and a great dinner. The highlight of the tour was the Uyuni Salt flats and Sandy went out of our way to ensure everything went smoothly and we got great photos. The car was great and we had our bags stowed in the boot (not on the rooftop). It was pretty spacious for 4+1 but the air con was a bit dusty. review_text: The tour to Casablanca vineyard, Viña Del Mar and Valparaiso with Lucho from Travitur is amazing. In Viña Del Mar we went to a manor called mansion Rioja, we saw an original aboriginal sculpture from Rapa Nui, we also got to see a Rodin sculpture in a Park, the beautiful flower clock, the sea lions on the beach and had a delicious meal at a restaurant with an impressive view of the beach. In Valparaiso we saw the navy building, the docks, a statue for an admiral with an everlasting flame, the funicular (cable car), and many bars and alleys in the graffiti urban landscape of Valpo. review_text: 2 days in Pucon and rain will keep us off the volcano bith days. Decided to catch the local bus to the National Park and hike the Los Lagos trail to the three lakes. Despite the drizzle / light rain it was an enjoyabke walk, if a bit wet. In our group we had the very fit hikers in proper boots to the not-so-fit in sneakers. All made it to Lago Verde, the furtherest lake in a little over two hours. We only made a few stops as rain meant we couldn't get the cameras out. The hike back down was muddy and slippery. The walks to the waterfalls add less than 10 minutes each and we all made it back down after a short lunch stop (10 minutes) for the 2.20 pm bus back. If the rain is heavy I wouldn't bother as you won't be able to see anything at the very few view points and the track will be horrible. Wish we could have been here in warmer, drier weather.

review_text: This tour was disappointing, largely due to the tour guide, Maria. It did not feel like a guided tour, more like an organized itinerary and transportation. It paled in comparison to our free walking tour the day prior and honestly could not be classified as a guided tour. Beginning with the itinerary itself, the Viña Del Mar portion felt like an add on. The two stops were superficial, solely for the photo opp, and you don’t get the opportunity to walk around or explore at all. The Valparaiso portion did feel like a decent amount of time and the vineyard was a nice addition if you like wine tasting. Although, be aware that the tasting only covers two wine samples. From the beginning, Maria’s actions did not inspire confidence. The pickups did not go smoothly and took longer than necessary because she wasn’t sure where/who she was picking up. Additionally, she wasn’t organized on the tour itself. Once we got to Valparaiso for the walking tour, she didn’t seem like she knew where she was going or had a plan. She had to stop to withdraw money because she didn’t have cash for the funicular. She repeatedly asked us where we wanted to go in Valparaiso, i.e., which street we wanted to go down; this defeats the purpose of a tour. Additionally, her English abilities were not sufficient to lead a tour in English. She was able to communicate basic facts but nothing more complex. We asked specific questions about the history of the port and significance of the graffiti and street art, but she wasn’t able to elaborate any further than what we already knew in our very basic understanding of Valparaiso culture and history. When she did point things out it was just to say this is so and so’s house but with no further information about the context or significance. She seemed more interested in making small talk than sharing information. Rather than sharing interesting facts and tidbits about history and culture, she shared personal information instead, not limited to family, birthdays, and personal opinions questioning the validity of graffiti as street art. One of the reasons we decided to do a guided tour was because we had been cautioned about the safety of walking alone in Valparaiso. However, if you speak Spanish and are decently savvy and are able to get around on your own would recommend exploring the city without a tour as you’d likely be able to do/see more on your own. We felt no safer with Maria due to her disorganization and clear unfamiliarity with the city than if we had been on our own. She almost left someone behind and had to be reminded by another person on the tour. She didn’t seem to realize we would all want to stop for lunch because she had taken us to a subpar empanada place for a quick snack. For lunch she took us to a street that she herself was unfamiliar with and was unable to provide recommendations other than reading the menus to those who did not understand Spanish. For the price we paid we expected a knowledgeable tour guide. We booked the tour because we read all of the excellent reviews of tours guided by other people, but we did not share this experience. It felt like this was Maria’s first time guiding a tour in Valparaiso. Unfortunately, we think this could have been an excellent tour with the appropriate tour guide. The driver was excellent and we felt very safe. It was convenient to have transportation and not have to navigate the bus system from Santiago to Valparaiso and the metro from there to Viña Del Mar, however, if you are well travelled, speak Spanish, and are decently comfortable traveling on your own, would recommend proceeding without a tour. That’s what we would have done in retrospect. However, we may have felt differently with a different tour guide. Review of: Valparaiso Port and Vina del Mar Full-Day Tour from Santiago

review_text: My wife and I have been blessed with the opportunity to visit many wineries across Chile, some of them with a visitor's center infrastructure way more developed than De Martino. That said, this winery and the tour around it are by far one of our favorites. The private tour we opted for has a cost of CLP 17,800 (USD 26) for individuals doings a normal tasting (3 wines - 1 standard reserve and 2 premium) whereas individuals just doing the tour pay CLP 8,000 (USD 12). María Jesús is the woman who pretty much handles the visitor center at De Martino. She is indeed a very knowledgable person on wine but it is very much up to the visitors to ask questions. As with any tour María Jesús does have an interesting script of what to say while visiting the fields (including a trial pit), the warehouse, the cellar and the winemaking area. However, it is when you start interacting more with her that you get to realize much there is to know about winemaking and the wine business. We felt we learned a lot from her. After the 1.5 hour tour is pretty much over, you are headed to a tasting room. María Jesús allowed us to figure out the wines by ourselves without imposing her views and what each wine should be. She gave us time and space, which allowed us to enjoy the tasting as a learning experience and/or just as a fun moment enjoying some very good wine. 100% recommended. Dear Ignacio, We really appreciate your comments and we are very glad that you enjoyed your visit at De Martino!, that you and your wife learnt something with us after visiting several wineries and enjoyed our wines! Cheers!

review_text: To understand Chile today it is necessary to take the time to go through this museum and follow the history of the Pinochet coup and the slow return to democracy in Chile. The museum is set up so you follow the history sequentially over time and it takes at least 2-3 slow hours to make your way through. It becomes emotionally draining (e.g. listening to people describe being tortured) and you naturally want to hurry on to the presumed "happy ending". But the ending doesn't come all that easily - for example, you learn that Pinochet never really paid for his crimes. Follow the whole story through to the end, it's worth the time. Some notes: first, if you don't speak and read Spanish you have to get an Audioguide or you will miss a great deal. Second, don't go on Mondays - it's closed.

review_text: I'd highly recommend the Navimag ferry from Puerto Natales to Puerto Montt. I did the 4 night, 3 day trip in May 2012. I thoroughly enjoyed it, but, having read the reviews below and based on a few comments from fellow passengers, I think a lot depends on what your expectations are. To enjoy it, I think you have to be interested in a fairly slow, calm journey through the magnificent fjords simply enjoying the views when the weather is good. If you're looking for constant activity and excitement plus, you're going to be disappointed. It's RELAXING! I was actually surprised when one of my fellow passengers said to me, "The scenery is all the same!" with the clear impression that he was bored. I couldn't relate as I thought the scenery was magnificent, and I found it wonderful to sit on board the boat and watch the world/scenery pass by. Many of the passengers found the section through the Pacific and the Bay of Paynes (?) to be rougher than they would have liked and ran to their beds. I didn't think it was that bad, but very few folks were out and about - and it's lots worse on other crossings from what our guide said. There were presentations every afternoon - both in English and Spanish - on the wildlife and history of the fjords. One thing I would say was a problem with Navimag was their communication before the trip. My information said the boat left at 6 am so I planned on getting there one hour beforehand. Only by chance did I learn that we had to board the night before at 9 pm. I'd recommend contacting Navimag before your trip to find out any particular boarding instructions. I think the times change based on the tides and when they need to pass through certain channels at high tide.

review_text: To set the stage: We had just arrived in Santiago from Valparaiso, via a wonderful guide service from Valparaiso, Mini Trole, who took us on a wonderful winery tour in the Casablanca Valley at Emiliana Winery before dropping us off at our hotel, the Vespucci Suites. After checking in to this very nice hotel we started looking at tour brochures in the lobby for tours of the Concha y Toro winery. We decided on Turistik's tours. We had the front desk call to make reservations for us for a tour the next afternoon. We wanted the front desk to call so there would be no confusion on details due to the language issue, we don't speak very good Spanish. First problem was the tour wan not available at the brochure price of $29,000 CHP! (about $44 US each). We were told the new price was $32,000 CHP (about $50 US ea.) We agreed to the new price and were charged immediately on our Visa card. We were told to be in the lobby promptly at 1:45 PM the next day for our tour pick up. We were very much looking forward to the tour so were in the lobby at 1:35 PM, 10 minutes early! By 2 PM when no one had arrived we asked the front desk to call for us and when they did they were assured we would be picked up momentarily. We were finally picked up at 2:45 PM with no excuses or apologies at all! We were shuttled a mile to a large bus depot where we were told to wait until we were called for the 2:30 PM Concha y Tora tour, and at that time it was 3:10 PM! We finally boarded a very full bus for the 45 minute ride to the winery. Upon arrival at 4:15 PM we were given our passes for our English tour and told to be back on the bus by NO LATER than 5:30 PM or the bus would leave without us! We had a nice tour of the winery, though rushed because of our late arrival. After the tour we barley had time to grab an additional glass of wine and a quick appetizer.We wanted to stop in the winery store to purchase some of the fine wines we had tasted but didn't have the time if we were to be on the bus by 5:30 PM as instructed. Upon getting on the bus at 5:25 PM we noticed that there were quite a few people missing that had arrived with us. By 5:45 PM when these people had not arrived on the bus we asked our guide what was happening. She said that 8 people had taken the Spanish only tour that included an additional wine tasting with the wine maker! She said we were not offered that additional tasting, which by the way was at no additional cost, because it was for Spanish speaking guests only! As if that wasn't enough, these last Spanish speaking guests didn't show up at the bus until 6:45 PM! To add insult to injury there were no apologies or offers of a credit to all those who were stuck on that bus for an hour waiting for those ill mannered guests! When we arrived at the bus depot for our transfer back to our hotel we again had to wait 30 minutes! We arrived at our hotel just before 8 PM! Please do yourself a huge favor, and tell all your traveling friends, DO NOT book any tours through Turistik Tours in Santiago, Chile! We appreciate your comment dear traveler, it is very important for us to know about your experience.

review_text: On a brisk morning in the spring month of October, we met our guides out of Kayak Sin Borders arranged by Tierra Patagonia. After a quick trip to Lago Grey and a quick bathroom stop at Hotel Grey, we were treated to an hour of how to out on a dry suit to go kayaking. A combination of pilates, yoga, and mechanical engineering resulted a sealed dry suit that would deter anyone from even mentioning the need for another restroom stop. The next 1.5 hours gliding along the mirror like waters of Lago Grey between and next to ice bergs was heaven on earth. We had the entire lake to ourselves and only the sounds of crackling ice bergs broke the tranquil silence. The subsequent journey down River Grey along class I rapids (maybe class .5 rapids) finishing at a wonderful picnic with panoramic views ended the amazing day. A rare and unique day without any wind in Patagonia, with photos that are unreal, was comparable to the Base of the Tower Hike as the highlight of our entire trip. What an amazing world!

review_text: Our B&B host in Valparaiso found Ritoque Expeditions and arranged for a ride the following day for my husband, myself and our 2 teenage daughters. An easy 30 minute drive from Valparaiso, the location is spectacular - high on a hill with 180 degree views of the ocean and beautiful sunsets. We wanted to stay overnight in Concon but couldn't find a hotel or cabina to our liking or budget. Owners Maria Elena and Sabastian (who are refreshingly on the "hippy" side) offered their guest cabin for $60 US but warned it was rustic. Upon arriving at this wonderful destination, we were greeted by a few friendly dogs, cats & ducks. Maria Elena explained that one of the ducks had bonded with dogs and followed them everywhere. There was also a litter of piglets that entertained us with their games, a new hatch of chicks and then the horses, of course! We felt like extras in a Dr. Doolittle movie! We LOVED the guest cabin, which was built out of many recycled materials. If you are visiting Valpo - stay here instead. It has 2 bedrooms, a living room, kitchen, full bath, sleeps 7. It is not luxury accommodations, but is clean and very comfortable. The gardens are filled with flowering plants, shade trees and the patio is very inviting to sit and relax. You will not regret staying here! Sabastian & Maria Elena went out of their way to make us feel like family. The horseback ride through the dunes, forest & beach was a day we will not forget (and I didn't even get sore!) Thank you for your comments on Trip Advisor, taking the time for commenting your experience with us means a lot for us, it helps us doing things better! When ever you are around Valparaiso again...WELCOME!!

review_text: When we stopped in Curacautin, we had the chance to stay at Epu Pewen. We remember it as such a great experience as it s now our favorite hostel in Chile. Epu Pewen is simply an outstanding hostel, the owners Suyaï & Jose Miguel, and theirs employees make a huge difference thanks to their kindness & hospitality. Ideally located in Curacautin, few miles away from national parks Conguillio, Tolhuaca and the national reserve Malalcahuello, it is the best option to discover the area. The hotels inside the national parks are really expensive. If you would like to go for a trekking or rafting in the parks you can ask for information at the travel agency in the hostel. Epen Pewen is a sustainable hostel where recycling is a rule which is really unusual in Latin America. Rooms are spacious and really pleasant. The very-high quality bedding has nothing to envy to five-starred hotels. The kitchen is fully equipped and decorated with a vintage/Mapuche style which is a favorable feature. Regarding cleanliness, Epu Pewen is the most cleaned hostel we have stayed in. Common areas and rooms are meticulously cleaned every day. Suyaï & Jose Miguel will do their best to make the most of your stay and even in the worst case scenario. We can tell as we had a car accident on our first day. They supported us so much that we were sad to leave at the end of our stay.

review_text: After running the Santiago marathon, we traveled to the Termas for some much needed relaxation. It was off-season for the most part, Chilan is pretty big ski town so there was lots of peace and quiet. The hot springs fill the pools and are quite amazing to lounge in, especially to relax some sore muscles. After a few days of rest and cervesas, we ventured into the Andes....on horseback. If you get the chance, definitely take the longest trip you can. We did a half day trip. The trails are challenging but the horses and guides are excellent and very little riding experience is necessary. There are spectacular views and vistas that you see in the movies and quite an adventure can be had.

review_text: This was a great day trip out of Santiago and into the Andes. We had a small group, only three of us, and our guide. After being picked up, we started driving out of Santiago and stopped at a gas station for breakfast/bathrooms. During the drive we were told about the history of the area. Once we arrived, we hiked for about an hour and a half to a spot where we had lunch and relaxed for a bit, taking in the views. Then took the hour and a half hike back. There are a couple brief areas of elevation at the beginning, but most of the hike is relatively easy. There was a lot of walking over loose rocks. We wore tennis shoes and were fine. Part of the terrain was fine dirt, we got quite dusty. Be prepared to use a “natural bathroom” if you need to go. Overall we enjoyed this trip and would recommend for anyone looking to get out of the city and experience the mountains. Review of: Andes Day Volcano 8K - Cajón del Maipo

review_text: We chose this company and did ignore at our own peril some poor reviews. We were to have a transfer for 3 couples who got together via Cruise Critic. We were the original organisers so paid a 1/3 deposit up front. Our correspondence with Fabiola at the company were answered quickly and professionally up to the date of the departure. We were waiting in the hotel lobby prior to the time we were to be picked up. Half an hour after the scheduled time for pick up, we contacted the other couple, whom we had not actually met, to see if they had been picked up. No. So we attempted to contact South Excursions and it was just going to voice mail. One hour later, we received a reply from Fabiola who said to us that there had been a flat tyre and they would be there in the next half hour. When we contacted the other couple they had been told there had been a traffic jam, so we agreed to text each other about further developments Finally 2 1/2 hours late we were picked up. On the way to pick us up the driver had apparently gone the wrong way down one way streets and even during a phone call to us refused to take directions from the hotel staff. We finally found out that the driver and guide were lost! They even had a satnav that they did not even connect. Fabiola spoke to us and said we wouldn't be charged for the tour of Valparaiso! Of course we couldn't fit it in as we were close to missing the ship embarkation time that we wanted. She met us at the port and still charged us the outstanding amount and gave each couple a bottle of cheap wine and chocolates. During the transfer the guide did not say one word apart from what she had to and they even had to ask us at the port which cruise ship we were sailing on as there were several in port that day. Upon our respective return we requested a refund and after some negotiations we did receive a refund several weeks after we returned home.

Remember to get your picnic bag and water, since there's no store inside the park

review_text: Maria picked me up from my hotel at 9am and we had a wonderful conversation about the region's history and geography on our way to the horses. We arrived at a secluded river house and met Luis, another guide who accompanied us on the trek. Luis drove us across the river in his speedboat, to where the horses were tethered. I was introduced to mine, Cassamares (probable spelled incorrectly due to my poor Spanish) who was a gorgeous and well-tempered male. We began our trek through the forest, fields and up hillsides, crossed streams and ended up at a beautiful waterfall after around 2 hours. The trek was incredibly beautiful and Maria was an excellent guide, telling me all about the flora and fauna of the area in great detail. We took some photographs by the waterfall and continued up the hillside on horseback. We finished the 4 hour ride with a very fast canter, which was exhillarating to say the least (this was a request from myself as I have a history of horse riding, but is not mandatory for less confident riders! The trip is very tailored to your ability and Maria is very easy to confide in if you are feeling nervous at any point, and can provide excellent advice and guidance about riding if needed!). Maria and Luis then cooked a marvellous BBQ with wine and dessert, before I was dropped back at my hotel at around 6pm. I cannot recommend this trip enough, Maria speaks excellent English and was extremely friendly, not to mention informative about the area! The location was surreal, exceptionally beautiful and a top location for a horse ride, the horses were very well behaved and made me feel very safe (as did the guides!). The BBQ was delicious, and overall this tour is incredible value for money. Thank you Maria and Luis for an unforgettable trip in Puerto Varas - I look forward to many more in the future! Dear Holly. It has been a real pleasure to meet you and show you this amazing ranch. I hope to see you next year . Good luck! Maria.

review_text: The Antarctica 21 experience was amazing all the way through !!! Everybody knows Antarctica has unpredictable weather due to the high winds so sometime it's a matter of luck and we were extra lucky as we had an extra day as plane that took us from Punta Arenas to Frei Station had to leave on Day 1 which is normally spent in Punta Arenas for briefings and sorting out boosts that they provide on loan for everyone (free). The staff was amazing ushering us and sorting out boots and everything on the go. Honestly having a 2 hour flight as opposed to 2 day journey through the Drake passage is a game changer. Allows you to enjoy the trip form start to finish with nothing but highlights. Basically 4 days compressed in 4 hours! Plus the 75 passenger planes are painted like penguins what's not to love ! We managed to go to lots of very different spectacular locations with the most epic views and amazing wildlife: dozens of humpback whales around the ship at times, orcas swam right next to the ship one afternoon, we saw 3 types of penguins (chinstrap, gentoo and adelie), leopard seals and many birds (skuas, sheathbills, cormorants, etc)! The crew was absolutely outstanding, I was utterly amazed by everyone and their life stories that they shared giving short presentations through out the journey (AJ went to the north and south pole skiing!, Nico climbed a mountain in Antarctica in crazy conditions, Steve made a wild polar bear sit and so many other crazy stories!). Since it was xmas the staff did a little dance and song show which was adorable! The cabins were very confortable and large with a really nice warm shower with great pressure (essential!). The food was very good and considering I'm vegetarian I had many great options for the buffet breakfast and lunch as well as really outstanding 3 course meals in the evenings. And finally the polar plunge (basically taking the shortest dip ever in the Antarctic) was a great way to end the journey with yet another great memory that I will cherish forever. What can I say I just loved every second of it :) Dear odi2k, Thank you very much for sharing your experience, we're very happy to read that you had such an incredible journey and that you enjoyed this beautiful continent! It seems like you had great luck as well with all the wildlife sightings! At Antarctica21, we're very happy to have such an exceptional team of expedition guides, we make sure to always have a variety of specialized backgrounds, who are also passionate about the region, and experts in guiding our travelers to the best sites. The polar plunge is definitely a great experience as well, I'm happy that you decided to join that adventure! Thank you again for sharing your experience with us!

review_text: A short ~20 minute drive from San Pedro, Lunar Valley offers a lot of photo ops. Landscape is barren (no vegetation) and hiking paths are sandy. One of the driest places on earth. Some of the paths that hike up the rock formations are VERY precarious. I'm an avid mountaineer, and was surprised at the lack of safety railings and/or grandmothers and little kids. If you lose your balance, you *will* fall and die. (I managed in flip flops, NOT recommended). If you're in the area, I recommend visiting. Sunset is particularly beautiful. Better than the lunar valleys in Peru and Bolivia.

review_text: 5-Star Review: Maipo Valley Wine Tour with Oscar & Rameses What an unforgettable day exploring the Maipo Valley with our fantastic driver, Oscar, and our incredibly knowledgeable and engaging guide, Rameses! review_text: Staff were excellent, with a good fun vibe. Good equipment meant we didn't get too cold despite the rain and freezing water. We were having a lot of fun so wanted to continue for longer! Hello Clare Thank you very much for your opinion about the trip on the Petrohue river. We depend on the water level on the river as we raft on a free flowing river. Levels depend on the rain and snowmelt we have. These months have been very wet and the river very high. This amount of water makes 1h40 trip much faster when you have twice more water. The flow pushes us faster and at the same time it is harder to get to eddies to stop. And last but not least, when temperatures are not that high we do spend much less time jumping in the water and swimming around with our guests than we do in summer time. Hope it helps. Thank you again. Richard Carrier

review_text: This review is for our all-day tour of the Lagunas Altiplanicas and Salt Flats. I want to first say that this review is in no way reflective of our driver, Miguel, who was very professional. However, our tour guide, Nicole, was awful and made the entire day miserable. Nicole arrived to pick us up at 7:15 AM (we were told pick up was between 6:30-7:00 AM). She did not apologize for the late arrival. We then rode around San Pedro for another 30 minutes, doubling back and forth for guests who apparently had overslept. During this whole time, there was no explanation for the driving back and forth, nor an apology. When a young woman from another hotel asked if there might be additional room in this van (there was an empty seat), Nicole curtly told her, “no!” and slammed the door. The entire time we were waiting, Nicole offered no explanation of why we were stopped. When I asked her in Spanish about why we were waiting and at what time we would return this evening, she told me to “calm down” and refused to give me an answer. I was left speechless - this was literally our first hour into the tour. She insulted my mother’s hearing later on by implying she couldn’t hear her explanations. She would frequently give a detailed explanation in Spanish, but incredibly short explanations in English. I’m bilingual and noted the significant difference in her commentary. There were also times while we were driving in which she would point out notable things in Spanish, but wouldn’t bother to translate for the 6 others on the tour who didn’t speak Spanish. Above everything else, we were originally told the tour would return around 4 PM. Instead, we were back in San Pedro at 6:15 PM. This was problematic because we had booked an evening tour that departed at 6:30 PM. Thankfully, we raced over and made it just in time. All in all, it was an unfortunate experience. I live in Chile and am used to things being a bit late, the Spanish and English translations being a bit different, etc. But this woman’s behavior was completely inappropriate and left a horrible impression on all of us, especially on my mother and sister who are visiting Chile for the first time. review_text: I decided to do something a little different for New Years this year and I looked into booking an adventure vacation somewhere I'd never visited before. I ended up picking a whitewater rafting vacation with H2O Patagonia on the "Futa" river and had one of the best vacations of my life. The scenery was beautiful and ever changing. We hiked in the Andes, got to raft some pretty powerful rapids on the Futa and even do some inflatable kayaking on a nearby river. Each day was a new experience and a new challenge, but each night it was really nice to return to the camp with its wood burning hot tub and truly amazing food and views of the snow capped andes and the sound of the river below. The best part of the trip, other than the amazing people I met at the lodge and the sights and adrenaline rush of whitewater rafting, was definetly the staff at H2O. They pampered us all at every chance and always made sure everyone was having a good time. The guides were especially exceptional, and made me feel very safe, even on class IV and V rapids! To anyone looking to travel in Patagonia I definetly recommend Futaleufu and H2O Patagonia.

review_text: We spent am amazing two days in December with Tom Taylor (the owner of Bodega Wine Tours) and his driver, Alberto. Tom is originally from the UK, but has lived in Chile for six years and forged excellent relationships with winery owners during this time. He does both group and private tours. He is fluent in English and Spanish. We arranged two days of private touring in advance. We appreciated his thorough and detailed planning and advance communication. His pricing is incredibly reasonable. Tom picks you up at your hotel (for us this was the Santiago Airport Holiday Inn) and delivers you back to your hotel at the end of the day. He picked us up at 8:00 each day and returned us around 4:30. Transportation is a very comfortable six seat van. The first day we toured three wineries in the Casablanca Valley and had a delightful lunch. (On private tours, the cost of the tastings and lunch are not included in the tour price. On group tours, the cost of the tastings is included. Not sure about cost of lunch on group tours.) Tom's tours are extremely reasonable in cost either way. In the Casablanca Valley he took us to two smaller boutique wineries first. We had amazing tastings with nuts, cheese and crackers. Got to explore the vineyards. Wine was amazing; huge pours. At the first winery we tasted both their pinot noir and chardonnay. At the second winery we tasted 7 different wines. We rounded out the tastings with a visit to a large producer (Quintay-a consortium formed by twenty different grape growers). Tasted eight wines there. The contrast between the small and larger producers was quite interesting. We finished up the afternoon with lunch at Casabotha restaurant. The next day we toured the Maipo Valley. Again we visited two boutique wineries and met their owners. We thoroughly enjoyed tasting their wines (Malbecs and two blends) and hearing about their operations. Very generous wine pours, delicious cheese, nuts and crackers to accompany the tastings. Both owners were so hospitable. The final winery visit was DiMartino (a large producer). Very nice tasting there as well with some unique wines. Lunch at Zinfandel Restaurant. We highly recommend Bodega Wine Tours. Tom and Alberto make the visit fun and educational. Tom caters to your every need or request. If you are visiting Santiago and want to do a wine tour, Bodega Wine Tours is the only way to go. ENJOY!

review_text: If your dream is to see the Milk Way and nearby galaxies on naked eye, you will need more than Atacama super-clear skies and dim city lights: you will need as little moonlight as possible. Even a quarter moon can spoil the dream of perfect observation. The standard tour runs from 9:00pm to close midnight in any condition of moonlight except full moon. So the perfect night vision is not warranted. If you get disappointed with the moonlight during the tour hours, there is a hint that the guides do not always share: acquire an Astronomy app, search for the hours when the moon is below the horizon (maybe 3:00 or 4:00am...) and simply get out of your hotel room at that time and look above. It may give you a view closer to your expectation. If your interest is in information, in a brief naked eye observation, and in the opportunity to see a few deep sky objects through the telescope, all packed in a 2-3 hours experience, this tour is for you. Most interesting above all is the lecture about how different cultures (including Andean cultures) figured the sky objects.

review_text: We went with a Show Travel tour (based in Iquique) and spent 12 hours in the park between driving and visits. It was amazing; geysers, thermal baths, mountains, volcanoes, pueblos and so much wildlife and unexpected vegetation in different parts of the park. We saw all 4 types of South American camelids! And flamingos! I recommend going with a tour guide who can explain the history of this region, the Inca presence, the significance of its wildlife and fauna, and the story of the indigenous people who cared for and respected this land and continue to do so today. You won't see many other tourists and you can truly get a slice of life in the desert. Unfortunately it's not a well protected park, which allows tourists to litter and get stupidly close to the historic and impressive petroglyphs. If you go, please respect this space and its beauty. Be sure to pack water and snacks as food is hard to come by. Highly recommended.

review_text: I highly suggest seeing Glacier Grey when visiting Torres del Paine. It was the highlight of Patagonia. There is a hotel on Lago Grey that has a boat that goes out a couple of times a day. You have to hike down to the beach, walk a rickety bridge to a dingy that takes you out to a larger boat. The boat takes off and you see enormous blue and clear pieces of ice floating in the milky grey waters. The surrounding Andes mountains are breathtaking and weather changes constantly. As the clouds move, more mountains appear. It was probably a 4 hour excursion. The boat takes you through the icy, grey waters to the glacier. Then you all toast your Pisco Sours with the glacier ice in your glasses! I'll never forget this day.

review_text: Our guides Esteban and Carlos were fun and energetic but we were a group of 12 and felt that 2 guides were not enough. We did make it to the summit which was awesome but felt a little rushed “we need to go faster guys” and on the way down some of us did not feel well and the guides just motored on without checking on us too much “it is normal to feel sick”. We felt they wanted to get us down quick as the rest of the group who didn’t summit were waiting hours at the bottom. They needed more guides or another vehicle for a group that size. review_text: We loved this cooking course, it was really great fun and one of our highlights of our South American trip. Ines the teacher met us at the top of the Acensor (recommend taking a cab if the Acensor not working as was the case when we were there) as planned and walked us the short way to the school. Ines in short was really excellent. She helped us to make empanadas with local salsa type dip (wow they were great), a vegetable and meat stew - very tasty, and a very simple dessert that we had never tried before and was a great fresh end to the meal. Along the way we also made an authentic Pisco Sour and the lunch we made and ate together was served with a nice Chilean Red wine. The food was great and knowing that we had helped make it was very satisfying. We were a small group which we enjoyed, and I think this helped Ines teach us so much more than cooking. We learned so much about Chile, the people, how they live, all about places, culture, food, education, way of life.... it was fantastic and more than we learned from any guide book. It was exactly what I had hoped we might also get and more- so it was great great fun. I'll definitely be making some of the dishes at home, we got the recipes afterwards and I can't wait to make the empanadas (my favourite). Martin the owner also swung by to say hello which was cool and again gave us another insight into chilean life esp for a foreigner. We loved it - you should book it and go you couldn't regret it.

review_text: We booked three tours with Turistik during our stay in Santiago. We booked the tours from the desk in our hotel. We did a private half day City Tour the first day and a private half day tour to Valle Nevado. Our guide was Marcelo and our driver was Jorge for both of tours. Marcelo is a wonderful guide. We learned so much from him. The City Tour includes a lot of walking, which was enjoyable after a long travel day to Santiago. Jorge is a great driver. Valle Nebado is a ski resort in the Andes Mountains. The drive to Valle Nevado is full of switchbacks and is also very narrow, but Jorge handled it well. We were lucky enough to see Condors while at the top of the mountain. There was time to walk around to go higher up on the mountain to get a better view of the glaciers. We wanted to get out of the city and into the Andes Mountains, so this tour for us was perfect. My third trip was a group tour to Isla Negra to see the Neruda house, and the Matetic Vineyard. The tour was very organized and very enjoyable and both destinations were worth the tour. The Neruda House sits on edge of the ocean with a beautiful view. The house is full of furniture, artwork and 1950s furniture. The Matetic Vineyard is very interesting because their winery practices biodynamic and organic agriculture, so there is a lot to learn. There was time to have a nice lunch outdoors and walk around the property. The only negative that I can say about this group tour was the time spent before the tour and after the tour for general transportation to the destination. I guess that is inherent in a group tour setting. Thank you for your comment. We are very pleased to have been able to deliver an excellent service. In Tursitik we want our passengers to return to their home with good memories and experiences of their visit to our country. See you soon. Turistik Team

review_text: The best way to explore the Atacama Desert and the Altiplano is with Raices Andinas. We did a 5-days tour in the North of Chile. Already our start in Arica with the first stop at the agricultural market of the city and later at the great museum of San Miguel de Azapa prepared us best for the things to come. We spend the following two days on the Altiplano 3500 – 4600 m above the sea level, discovering salt lakes and abounded villages. On the fourth day we made our way down to the Atacama Desert and stopped, for example, at the oasis of Pica or the Oficina Salitrera Humberstone. A ghost town in the middle of the desert, before heading to Iquique on our last day. Orlando, our tour guide, did a great job. He took us with him to this stunning nature and landscape on the Altiplano, surrounded by active volcanos and wildlife. Besides, the turned our focus on several topics like the history of this region, the ongoing conflict between Chile and Bolivia, but also to the harsh living conditions of the indigenous people living on the Altiplano. He gave us the opportunity to meet to local people living far beyond any streets or villages and talk with them about their way of live and their traditions. He also continued patiently stopping at any Vicuna we met to take a picture and adapted the tour to our interests. With him we had the chance to learn a lot about the unique ecological system, the (geological) history of this place and the struggle to find the balance between preserving the nature and utilizing mineral resources. If you want to visit this amazing area then I recommend you Raices Andinas.

review_text: Patagonia is jam packed full of amazing hiking! Particularly, the Cerro Castillo day hike starting from the town of Villa Cerro Castillo is a great trail. The 3 pronged peaks of Cerro Castillo lends itself to comparison with its more well known 3 pronged counterpart. That would be Las Torres, which we were lucky enough to see on the W Trek. But with less people and hype, we hold this day hike in similarly high regard. There is a decent amount of information online about the multi-day Cerro Castillo circuit. But we are here to shed some light on the lesser known day hike option. Getting to Villa Cerro Castillo The day hike is easily walkable from the tiny town of Villa Cerro Castillo in Patagonia. If you are planning on travelling Patagonia south to north, hopefully you have visited Río Tranquilo for the incredible Marble Caves. From here, simply organise a transfer at the main bus station. In Patagonian summer as of February 2020, buses depart 8am daily heading to Coyhaquie via Villa Cerro Castillo for $10,000CLP ($12USD). Unfortunately, whether departing the bus earlier at Villa Cerro Castillo compared to the final destination of Coyhaique didn’t seem to change the price. But admittedly we should have questioned more before paying! The bus arrives into Villa Cerro Castillo around 10-11am. If you are not departing from Río Tranquilo, buses frequently head north from Cochrane to Villa Cerro Castillo on route to Coyhaquie. They should be easily booked with a day’s notice in town. Otherwise, if your trip is north to south, a bus should be easily organised from Coyhaquie to Villa Cerro Castillo. The Cerro Castillo day hike The Cerro Castillo circuit is often completed as a 4 day hiking trip. However, we had limited time in Patagonia. This day hike involves walking from the town of Villa Cerro Castillo to the laguna and back, measuring around 15km. It takes 5-6 hours. There is a steep elevation of 1.1km over 7.5km to reach the laguna There is varying consensus online as to where the Cerro Castillo day hike starts, and whether you have to pay or just jump the fence. As of February 2020, you must pay an entrance fee of $5,000CLP ($6USD) to landowners. This is because the beginning of the hike is on private farmland. You must also pay a separate $13,000CLP ($15USD) to the Reserva Nacional Cerro Castillo. The prices are extortionate for a day hike and may well put people off. However we assure you that the hike is worth it! In peak season, there are actually national park staff who will explain the trail to you before you set off. To be honest, having someone explain how to follow a trail was fairly unnecessary. It’s not rocket science! Nevertheless, the day hike itself is a very demanding uphill affair. There are phenomenal views back to Villa Cerro Castillo and the surrounding mountainous landscape on route to a stunning lagoon below the Castillo mountain.

review_text: Claire and Felipe are two wonderful, honest and caring people with a wonderful sense of adventure. I had the pleasure of spending two trek days with Felipe, the most memorable being a hike up Cerro Paine. What is really great about Felipe is his desire to share new places, off the beaten track with visitors. The day we had planned to hike up Cerro Paine we woke up to a fresh coat of snow in late September. We assumed our hike would be rescheduled, but Felipe assured us that if we were up to it we could still go. We were so excited for the adventure. We were told we needed to have really good sunglasses, preferably polarized, to avoid getting snow blind. I did not bring my best pair and was worried that they might not be enough protection. Felipe helped ensure that I had the right gear and made it possible for me to still make the hike. While Felipe is an experienced hiker and could likely hike the mountain in record time, he is a patient guide and makes sure that we keep a pace that we all can keep up and would encourage us to ask for breaks when ever we needed. He is an amazing teacher and guide, proper hiking takes certain skills, and a certain amount of patience if non-experienced hikers are to make it up such a challenging trek. We made it up past the tree line and almost at our first summit when we stopped for a lunch break. Felipe told us that in his professional opinion we should turn back, but it was not a matter of life and death so if we wanted to keep going we could tell him so. He could see the state of the snow covered mountain and knew it was going to be tough. During lunch the wind started to pick up and we decided to listen to the professional advice of our guide. The trek down to the tree line was scary since the wind was dropping the temperature and there was no cover. But through it all we had Felipe's calm voice telling us we were fine and just keep moving, one step at a time. We made it back to tree line and immediately it got warmer and we were all joking again. Through it all I knew I could trust Felipe with my life and I loved every minute of the adventure, at least in hind-sight. That evening we had dinner together and shared some hilarious stories. These two are smart and care about the nature around them. You can feel it in the way they talk about Chile and the wilderness they bring you to. If you are looking for something different and spiritually cleansing, I highly recommend booking some adventure with Madre Roca Patagonia. Hi Fredella! Thank you so much for such an awesome review! I still remember the Cerro Paine hike day! It was cold from lunch on! "Slowly and steady is the way!". I am glad you folks had fun and enjoyed Cerro Paine, as it is one of my favorite hikes in Torres del Paine National Park. In Madre Roca, we think that there can´t be tourism without taking care for Nature. That is why we are commited to skip the most popular and over crowded hikes in Torres del Paine National Park, and we will take you to the off the beaten trails Thanks again Fredella! Big hug to Eddie! Best, Felipe.

review_text: I booked a “Parks and Politics” bike tour; everything from emails to directions to the office were excellent. At the start of the ride, the guides emphasized safety and the bikes were easy to ride. However, I will only rate the tour as average: my issue was that there were numerous riders on the tour and whenever we stopped for a commentary by the guide it was almost impossible to hear him (the guide) due to traffic noise and many other riders crowding around, so unless you were very close to the guide it was impossible to hear. I was disappointed in the parks as I expected to see more space and greenery. Also, several of the venues were not open for visiting inside (renovations or day of tour closed); vendor could have used some ingenuity by adjusting the tour to include something like the market place to allow for the closed venues. I would gladly book again with the vendor but would select a different tour.

review_text: Recently refurbished and reopened, this relatively small museum contains some of the best pre-Columbian artifacts I have seen anywhere in the Americas, carefully selected and beautifully and intelligently displayed (and with signs in both Spanish and English). Begin by going down stairs to the more ancient and archeological past. Then go up the stairs, but instead of going straight ahead, notice that left and right are galleries that open off balconies around two interior courtyards. First walk around the balconies above the two courtyards and read the excellent explanatory signs for the galleries. Then enter the inside galleries from the balconies. If you enter the inside galleries from the central hall first encountered, you will miss these excellent explanations, or only find them later. The relatively small size of this museum—selective instead of exhaustive—is a real plus. Each display has the room it needs and you have the time to enjoy it all. Among the galleries, I found the textile room, in particular, a real stunner. Also, if you go on Sunday (as I did), not only will it be free, but you will have the pleasure of mingling with local families enjoying this view of their country's heritage.

review_text: We just returned from a three-weeks’ holiday in Chile; visiting Santiago, Atacama, Pucon, Puerto Veras, Eco Camp in Patagonia and Colchagua Valley. Despite beautiful scenery in Atacama and awesome experience in Torres del Paine, Pucon remains our favorite. Volcan Villarrica is spectacular and seemed to follow us wherever we went! Our congenial local guide, Agustin, is a committed environmentalist with a deep knowledge of flora&fauna as well as the culture of the indigenous Mapuche people. After a very pleasant first trek and a visit to Huife thermal springs, at short notice, we asked Agustin to organise another trek for us on the second day when he also suggested a boat trip to Isla Allaquilen on Lago Villarrica. It was a perfect end of our short stay as we were rewarded with blossoms scattered all over the island and a panoramic view at the top of the hill. Agustin is a perfect traveling companion, very attentive and went out of his way to make our trip a memorable one. Gracias por mostrarnos alguna cosa muy especial. We wish we could be back for the eclipse next year!

review_text: My husband and I booked a blind tasting and tour at the winery and were accepted even though we only booked it the night before. We were met at the entrance by our enthusiastic waving guide Marcello. First he took us out in the vineyard and showed us their grape vines and taught us to identify the different grapes by their leaves shape and color. Second we were brought into the cellars and were shown their tanks and barrels. Here we even got to drink wine out of the tanks. Lastly we were lead back up to their tasting area for a blind tasting of four wines that our guide Marcello even participated with us in. It was a really informative and fun way to try the wines without the labels and prices. We did end up guessing 2 of the 4 wines correctly. Along with the tasting we were served goat cheese and crackers and when we finished with the revealing of the wines we were told to take our time and to try more of any of the 4 wines. The wines are typical of the Colchagua region with Cabernet Sauvignon, Merlot, Carmenere, and Syrah making up the wines that we tasted. They all had a nice fruitiness and the wines that were grown at a higher altitude were more defined in taste and had a bit more structure. Along with the tour, and tasting we were also given 30% off of our bottle purchases. The price for the tour and tasting was a bit high at 18000 pesos ($25) for bottles of wine that were between 5500 and 11000 pesos. Although, the tour and blind tasting were so great and personal that it was totally worth it for someone who is interested in learning more about the wine and region of Colchagua.

review_text: San Pedro de Atacama hosts a lot of beautiful places. The Moonvalley of course, but definetely also te Rainbowvalley (Arcoiris), the Geysers of Tati, Salar Lagoon etc. etc. If you buy a tour the entrancefee for these places is not included so you always pay extra. You know this from advance so there is no problem.and what you get i named places is worth for your money. The Cejar Lagoon is different. You pay 15.000 pesos in the afternoon extra, which is more than 20 euros for a look at two hardly interesting pools. In one of which you can take a swim. It really is bizar if you compare it to all the other great things to see at a lower price. I'm told the indiginous people have the right to set the entrancefee and want to make sure the lakes stay in good condition. What they do actually is making a lot of money in return for nothing. So, my advice, stay away. Review of: San Pedro de Atacama: Half day Cejar Lagoon afternoon tour.
