review_text: We had the privilege of spending time on our own with Frederica for the first hour or so of this tour which took place solely in the vineyard, where she showed us several different varietals of vine of different ages (including some 127 years old) and different types of canopy management. She explained the various processes needed to tend to the vines including pruning methods. In all the years I have been visiting wineries in different parts of the world this was the most interesting and informative tour of a vineyard. The tour ended with tastings of Neyen Espiritu de Apalta 2011 and 2013, both of which were superb. Many winery tours concentrate on the process of converting grapes into wine which is of course interesting, but I would absolutely recommend this tour to learn about the cultivation of grapes. I should add that Frederica was not only knowledgeable and enthusiastic but also a delightful person to spend time with.

review_text: Matias and driver Vincente met us at the hotel at 7 am for our 8:15 flight from Punta Arenas to Porvenir. Matias is very knowledgeable and particularly an expert on Patagonian birds. Visitors are kept about 50 meters away from the colony. However, Matias brought binoculars and an optic scope which enhanced our ability to observe the penguins. We believe the flight option, although more expensive, is a much better experience than the taking the ferry to Porvenir.

review_text: This winery is owned by the same people as the casino... and the hotel... and the other main tourist magnets in Santa Cruz. While it's great that they're doing so much for tourism in the region, this winery is not meant for anyone other than those who want a pretty view and have time and money to burn. The view is spectacular, both from the main building and from the hill the tour finishes on, especially in the fall. The colors, clouds, hills, everything, really were breathtaking. However, the wine tour was unremarkable. I had the misfortune of having a guide (in Spanish) who mumbled through his speech and was quickly drowned out by the very machines he was attempting to talk about. The tasting followed, and while the wine cellar is beautiful, we had to stand for 30 minutes and used the same glass for each tasting. After the tasting, we headed up to the gondola to go up the hill. I had felt uneasy about this part of the tour, but I was really blown away by it all. While I understand the mentality of the owners - many tourists to this region are probably coming to Chile only for the wine and to see the vineyards and won't get a chance to go to the Araucania, Easter Island, or San Pedro de Atacama - this is the same family who made the great and very thorough museum in town, which offers a great deal of information on all of the above cultures and other Andean cultures without the gaudiness and tackiness of a fake Moai statue, or a fake Mapuche ruca, or llamas packed into a too-small corral. They would have been better off to focus their energy on creating a quality winery experience, and leave the cultural aspect to the museum.

review_text: My wife and I took this tour in December 2022 on our first day in Chile after arriving via an overnight flight. It was a nice introduction to the country. Communication via text was smooth beforehand. The breakfast and lunch, both hosted at the homes of locals, were a great touch. Christian was a capable guide loaded with information, not just about wine but about the area and its history. Very enjoyable day. One word of warning: This tour does not feature wine tastings per se. Rather, you show up at each of the four vineyards with a single, pre-purchased bottle of wine (or a bottle that your guide purchases in the moment) that you can enjoy on premises. Given the description, I had expected tastings at each vineyard. Instead of being served a variety of pours in a tasting room by someone who works at the vineyard, you drive up to various producers and open a bottle. That could be good or bad depending on your preferences. We also ended up being the only two people on the day's tour, which made for an intimate experience but also meant we were in the back of a sedan rather than the "little wine bus" in the description. Again, could be good or bad depending on your perspective. Overall we had fun. Christian shows you a great time and there are worse ways to spend a day in Santiago. But if you're looking for traditional wine tastings where you really get a sense of each vineyard, this might not be for you. Review of: Maipo Valley litle wine bus from Santiago Hello! review_text: Travel around South America and it's amazing the colonizers you run into. The Spanish, of course. But also the Portuguese, the English, the French and, yes, the Welsh, to name a few. In Frutillar, Chile, it's Germans. Museo Colonial Aleman (German Colonial Museum) honors those 1852-and-later immigrants with a park adjoining Lake Llanquihue (see my review, "On a clear day . . .") that recreates their way of life. Founded in 1981, the museum has a country house, a cemetery, a blacksmith's house, a bell tower and a water mill, all set on beautiful forest and gardened grounds (some of the trees are more than 100 years old). Most, if not all, of the items inside the houses are original (but relocated) objects. TIPS: * If you're pressed for time, head for the impressive country house and the fascinating old German cemetery near it.

review_text: Our tour of Chile was organised by Voyages Jules Verne. They arranged our private excursions in Atacama from our base in San Pedro over a five day period through Trekana Experience. This included airport transfers and visits over a 3 day period to Moon Valley, Ckari Lookout, Highland Lagoons, Chaxa Lagoon (Atacama Salt Flat), Tatio Geysers, Machuca, Putana Wetlands and White Geyser (for breakfast). During this time we had two guides both of whom were absolutely fantastic. They were extremely friendly, knowledgable, informative and professional. We were kept informed via a printed itinerary on arrival, our guide each day and text message updates the evening before noting any change to start times. Trekana picked us up and dropped us off at our hotel each day, assisted with baggage, ensured we knew of any important recommendations E.g. clothing, altitude etc. As some visits were at higher altitude where sickness may affect some they were especially attentive to ensure our well being. Our daily tours were packed with amazing and varied scenery, wildlife / bird sightings and an amazing lunch after visiting the salt flats and breakfast at White Geyser after our very early start to see the sunrise in the mountains. That breakfast was in one of the most awesome settings, such peace, tranquility and stunning view. Our guides brought the food and drink with them and set a table / bench and chairs up /- plenty of choice and very civilised. Our only negative comment was that there were others in our very small the group who didn’t get these messages directly, as Trekana treated us as group leaders rather than equals and separate couples. That said, everything worked well for everyone. However our strong recommendation to improve things is that Trekana set up WhatsApp groups from the outset including all participants to make life easier for everyone; especially when those in groups are not connected in any other way than by being part of a tour group. We appreciate Trekana guides’ experience and have many great memories that will remain with us forever. We know there is a lot of choice of tour / excursion operators in San Pedro, Atacama but we would highly recommend Trekana Experience.

For some of the older people in the group the walk to the boat was longer than they would of liked but I enjoyed it as I was at the front of the group enjoying a chat with one of our guides, Diego. The weather the whole day really was incredible, 25 plus degrees all day, dark blue cloudless sky's, no breeze or wind and perfect visibility. Obviously you get excited when you first see icebergs floating in the water and these Glaciers are some of the more detailed ones I've seen, I think you get one free drink, a Pisco Sour which I associate more with Peru, then you have to pay, I had a couple of beers. My Camera battery died half way through and after the Glaciers most people went inside but I stayed outside for the duration and admired the incredible scenery, I even enjoyed the walk back over the huge expansive beach to the entrance/coach, thoroughly enjoyed and a must if your there.

review_text: We chose Lithium for our 3 day tour of the Uyuni salt flats after reading great reviews and receiving a recommendation from a friend. We booked a few days in advance while in San Pedro. The logistics leading up to the tour were disorganized. We worked with a new employee who did not have all of the information we needed and gave us incorrect information (he even told us the wrong start time for the astronomy tour we also signed up for with lithium and we almost missed it). We were also not given all the information we needed about the border crossing into Bolivia. We finally got to speak to Eva, the most knowledgeable person in the office, but she was still unsure of many of these details especially regarding the visas we needed to enter Bolivia as US citizens. She eventually contacted the Lithium owner to help us find the answers but it was a frustrating and lengthy process. We were also assured by Eva multiple times that after the crossing we would remain with the same company. This was not the case and we were passed off to a Bolivian company called Estrella del Sur. This ended up being fine but it seems every tour company needs to pass you off to a partner company when you cross the border. That said, once we were on the tour, we couldn't have been happier with the experience. We were very nervous after reading reviews about unsafe driving and uncomfortable conditions but we found exactly the opposite to be true with our Lithium tour. Our guide, Omar, was excellent in driving cautiously (never over 40 mph), explaining each site and making sure we were all comfortable and happy. Food The food was of both higher quality and quantity than expected. We barely touched the snacks we packed. Each meal was hot and had both meat and vegetable options. Still a good idea to bring snacks and definitely bring a lot of water for all three days (1 liter per day per person) because this will not be supplied by the tour. Accommodations The first night we stayed in a hostel in a remote village. The 4-person rooms are shared and are made up so you don't need a sleeping bag. There are only three bathrooms for all ~20 guests and only one shower. The shower is bare bones and you need to pay to use it and for the hot water and towel (10 bolivianos for hot water and another 10 for towel). The hostel was rugged but fine. The second night we stayed at a salt hotel which was very nice (no sleeping bag needed). All rooms are doubles and you have the choice to pay extra (160 bolivianos) for a private bathroom. It is just 40 minute drive from the location you will watch the sunrise on the salt flats. Cost We were charged $175USD / person for the 3 days / 2 nights originating in San Pedro and ending in Uyuni (does not include transfer back to San Pedro). You will need to also pay for park entrance fees throughout the tour and will need to exchange Chilean pesos for bolivianos prior to the tour while in San Pedro. Schedule Here is a snapshot of the schedule to give you an idea of what you will see and what your days will look like: Day 1 7:10am-8:10am Pick up by bus at hostel in San Pedro de Atacama Drive 5 min review_text: This is within walking distance of the downtown. I would dare say it is just as good, if not in some respects better, than the Recoleta Cemetery in Buenos Aires. We noted that there is still space available for those so inclined to make a purchase, sea views optional. Many of the mausoleums are works of art, as in the Recoleta, but some here are complete with their own private chapels and have more space surrounding them than the ones that are cheek to jowl at the Recoleta. Very glad that we saw both as they each impart a flavour representative of their respective regions. Highly recommended for a visit.

review_text: Torres del Paine surely is the crown jewel of national parks and thoroughly deserves to be the 8th Wonder of the World. Its no wonder the Chileans work so hard to protect it! The park has it all. Vertical granite mountains, stunning glaciers, emerald-green forests, turquoise blue glacial lakes, icebergs, guanacos, condors, pumas. There is no shortage of things to see or do. Driving around the park... I cannot recommend hiring a car and driving around the park enough. I hired a car with a friend in Puerto Natales. It takes at least two hours to get to the park entrance from Puerto Natales and two hours to get back. If driving in from Puerto Natales, it will take a full day. Having done the W, I can say with confidence that some of the views from the road cannot be seen on the trek. Some of the views from the road are the most iconic of the park particularly of Los Cuernos ('The Horns'). The landscape views from Lago Pehoe and Salto Grande will break hearts! There are numerous other view points along the road. Views among the icebergs at Lago Grey at the end of the road are particularly stunning. Regarding the W trek... The W can be done from East to West or West to East. There are pros and cons for doing either. I spent five days going from East to West to get the hard ascent to the Torres out of the way. The views on the W for each day are varied with each view as unbelievably beautiful as the last. From East to West the high points are the Torres, Los Cuernos, Valle del Frances, Lago Pehoe & Glacier Grey. It is as if you are rewarded with a daily crescendo! The reputation of experiencing all seasons here is well deserved and impressive! In my 5 days of trekking the W, it rained, there was a blizzard, clear weather with sunshine and hurricane-force winds. Pack and dress appropriately! You can drink water from any stream or river in the park. There is no need to treat or filter the water. Its fresh & clean. There are refuges scattered along the W trek. They are comfortable, well-heated, serve hot meals & hot showers. Overall, excellent. Camping options are available in the park. There are designated camp sites along the W and around the refuges for $10 a night. However, if you are camping and some serious weather rolls in it might be worth thinking about spending the night indoors! Be aware though prices per night per person can be upward of $40 USD. It is impossible to get lost on the W. The trails are very well marked and you even get a map of all the trails as you enter the park. There is no need for a guide unless you are looking for information on the park, fauna & flora. If time allows, trek some of the trail called 'The Tail' along Lago Pehoe from Refugio Paine Grande. The views from the lakeside are gorgeous. I have never been to a place quite as special as Torres del Paine. In all my travels so far, it is the most beautiful place on Earth. Pack your bags & go!

review_text_preprocessed: Torres del Paine surely is the crown jewel of national parks and thoroughly deserves to be the 8th Wonder of the World. Its no wonder the Chileans work so hard to protect it! The park has it all. Vertical granite mountains, stunning glaciers, emerald-green forests, turquoise blue glacial lakes, icebergs, guanacos, condors, pumas. There is no shortage of things to see or do. Driving around the park... I cannot recommend hiring a car and driving around the park enough. I hired a car with a friend in Puerto Natales. It takes at least two hours to get to the park entrance from Puerto Natales and two hours to get back. If driving in from Puerto Natales, it will take a full day. Having done the W, I can say with confidence that some of the views from the road cannot be seen on the trek. Some of the views from the road are the most iconic of the park particularly of Los Cuernos ('The Horns'). The landscape views from Lago Pehoe and Salto Grande will break hearts! There are numerous other view points along the road. Views among the icebergs at Lago Grey at the end of the road are particularly stunning. Regarding the W trek... The W can be done from East to West or West to East. There are pros and cons for doing either. I spent five days going from East to West to get the hard ascent to the Torres out of the way. The views on the W for each day are varied with each view as unbelievably beautiful as the last. From East to West the high points are the Torres, Los Cuernos, Valle del Frances, Lago Pehoe & Glacier Grey. It is as if you are rewarded with a daily crescendo! The reputation of experiencing all seasons here is well deserved and impressive! In my 5 days of trekking the W, it rained, there was a blizzard, clear weather with sunshine and hurricane-force winds. Pack and dress appropriately! You can drink water from any stream or river in the park. There is no need to treat or filter the water. Its fresh & clean. There are refuges scattered along the W trek. They are comfortable, well-heated, serve hot meals & hot showers. Overall, excellent. Camping options are available in the park. There are designated camp sites along the W and around the refuges for $10 a night. However, if you are camping and some serious weather rolls in it might be worth thinking about spending the night indoors! Be aware though prices per night per person can be upward of $40 USD. It is impossible to get lost on the W. The trails are very well marked and you even get a map of all the trails as you enter the park. There is no need for a guide unless you are looking for information on the park, fauna & flora. If time allows, trek some of the trail called 'The Tail' along Lago Pehoe from Refugio Paine Grande. The views from the lakeside are gorgeous. I have never been to a place quite as special as Torres del Paine. In all my travels so far, it is the most beautiful place on Earth. Pack your bags & go!

review_text: We spent 9 fabulous days in and around Torres del Paine. I won’t add reviews of our time hiking in the park, as there are countless sites and blogs that offer incredibly useful and detailed information about trails and hikes to suit every interest. Our trip to the park began with 3 days in Puerto Natales. We checked in to Keoken Bed & Breakfast where Rodrigo guided us to things to see and do in the area. (A great place to stay near the lake and the center of town.) We rented a car from Newen Rent a Car. They are THE BEST company. Maria and her mother will deliver perfectly clean cars and add lots of information about the park and hikes in the area. The only thing we would have done differently is rent an SUV instead of a smaller car. The roads in the park are manageable without an SUV, but it would have been so much more comfortable and relaxing on those dirt roads (no paved roads in the park or leading to it for many miles from the south entrance at Serrano) in a larger vehicle. We spent the first 3 nights at Hotel Rio Serrano just outside the southwest entrance to the park. It’s a beautiful hotel in a perfect setting and offers great services. We did the bed and breakfast program instead of the very pricey all-inclusive plan that they offer. We had food with us from Puerto Natales, so ate a hearty breakfast that is offered at the hotel, a light packed lunch and sandwiches for dinner. The refrigerator in the room was a bonus, but we could have managed without it. The food in the park is absurdly expensive and not the reason for being there, so we felt good about our choice to create our own meals. The spa is a treat after long days hiking and included in your stay. Great weather (although really windy!) made for some great hikes in that end of the park. Then we spent 2 nights at Hotel Las Torres at the northeastern end of the park. The roads leading to this entrance from Puerto Natales are all paved but it is a longer journey than to the Serrano entrance - worth the extra miles and time to be on paved roads! We were already inside the park, so we traveled along the main park road toward the Laguna Amarga entrance. Hotel Las Torres is a working estancia where horses are set out to pasture and then corralled daily. It’s fun to watch. This is also the passing point for the Las Torres Mirador. We treated ourselves to the Lamb BBQ that was a meat lovers dream come true. From there we headed back to Puerto Natales for a night before making our way back to El Calafate. The park is magnificent and exciting. We avoided crowded hikes by starting early - 9:00 or so. We rarely ran into people along our hikes but noted the numbers arriving as we were leaving some areas. The greatest number of people appeared on the only section of the W route that we hiked from Hotel Las Torres along Nordensjkold Lake. It was fun to join them for awhile and then turn around and return to our cozy hotel. However you choose to see the park, you will not be disappointed.

review_text: I have visited many National Parks around the world, but none comes close to the fantastic scenery of Torres del Paine. The first time I saw the magnificent granite spires of the torres( towers ) and the cuernos (horns) , I was in awe!!! And, to see them at sunset is a photographer's dream! No photo can truly capture their magnificence. It is a site that does not disappoint, even after all the build-up it gets. It is not an easy task to get here, but well worth it! I stayed at Hosteria Pehoe, a small hotel in the middle of Lake Pehoe. It features great views of the mountain peaks( torres & cuernos). The hotel has a nice bar and a fine restaurant. Besides the incredible scenery, there is much else to photograph. The area has a high concentration of guanacos and nandu birds, which are quite photogenic. The only negative comment I can make about Torres del Paine is the weather. You can get all 4 seasons of weather in one day!! Plan your trip carefully, but definitely GO!!

review_text: If you go to Santiago, Cerro San Cristobal is a must. You´ll be able to see the whole city and also take quite nice photos of the Andes from there aswell. If you come during summer or when weather is warmer you'll be lucky enough to have no smog conditions (Smog is only a problem during Autumn & mostly all Winter except post rain days). Beware of robberies, especially if you climb via non transited routes. Plase take the roads, which are usually guarded and many people walk up and down all day long, so it´s very very safe. There´s a funicular aswell if you are lazy enough not to walk yourself up there. This funicular runs from the very lower part of the hill to the summit, with a stop for the Zoo in the middle. There are also 2 big botanic gardens, two public swimming pools a restaurant with the best city views. A down side is that the cable car system was shut down few years ago, so it´s not possible to get to the summit using this service which used to be a lot of fun... Make sure to bring your camera with you, do not litter and take care of this beautiful place. Do not smoke and throw your cigarrettes to the forest as it might cause a big fire.

review_text: Grey Glacier is an excellent contrast to the Perito Moreno Glacier. Where Perito Moreno is surrounded by tourist infrastructure, and is a very active glacier, Grey Glacier is the exact opposite. Before you even get to the glacier, you will see a landscape like nothing else. There is a large flat expanse in front of you which the glacier has carved out when it was much larger. This expanse is covered with skree and then you see the lake. The wind seems to roar down the lake from the glacier, ensuring you will receive an icy blast. However the wind also drives any large 'icebergs' down from the glacier to the edge of the lake. Its surreal and we took a double take to get our dimensions. From the hotel, you see the lake, and the large icebergs (many times the size of a house) right up near the edge of the lake. You then realise those little dots in front of you are people in the distance. Hard to describe but if you've been there, you'll know what I mean. You can walk or get a tour bus down to the lake departure point. A word of caution. The day we were there was a very windy day and the waves coming down the lake were very big. They do a transfer to the tour boat via smaller boats. The large waves meant you need to be careful. We did have one person fall within our group. Nothing serious, but its a remote place so be careful. The wind racing down the lake means that sometimes the tour boat gets canceled. I didn't find the ride excessively bumpy even though they were very close to canceling the day we were there. Its a bit of a journey (I guess it felt like about 40-50 minutes going to the glacier). The boat was comfortable enough and offered good protection from the weather. We weren't there in peak season but our trip was full. Once you get there, you'll see an impressive glacier. Our guide told us the glacier used to be much larger, and this was borne out by the surrounding landscape. This glacier is not calving constantly, however there are plenty of ice chunks floating near the edge. Its a great opportunity to get up close and the blue color is mesmerising. You'll get the obligatory scotch with 'glacier ice' (who knows if it is, just go with it) when you get there. The boat ride back was much faster as we virtually surfed the waves. All up, we enjoyed the whole experience and I recommend it.

review_text: One of my favorite things in Chile. ALMA is the reason why I traveled to the Atacama Desert part of Chile. The tour gets you up close and personal with the antenna control room and you might get a close-up of one of the out-of-service antennas. They've got a GREAT visitors center hallway, but it's underutilized. From the hallway you get a nice view of the antenna maintenance area and there are some interesting photos on the wall. But the hallway is so long and wide that it would be a GREAT place to put some multi-media, hands-on stations. The most challenging thing about running tours to ALMA is that you can't go to the antennas atop the mountain. That's where the REAL exciting stuff is. It would be fantastic if ALMA cold somehow figure out a way to get a pressurized bus up to the top of the mountain. I'd pay money to do that. The tour guide was VERY knowledgeable and answered every question. ALMA just started doing public tours, so they're still working out the bugs. The 40-minute bus ride from San Pedro de Atacama to ALMA could have been more productive. The tour guide was so knowledgeable that the ride would have been a great opportunity to pass some interesting information.

review_text: Its my favourite tour in Atacama. Its really unique. The tour starts at 5 am and ends at 12 pm. It cost usd$30 + ticket to national park usd$7. They pick you in your hotel and they take you straight to the geysers. Some considerations of what you have to bring. Water, sunblock, sun glasses, swimming suit, flip flops and towel. About your clothing you should use 2 pairs of socks, first layer of pants and shirt, thick pants, gloves, thick shirt, mountain jacket and something for your head and ears. Altitude there is 4.300 mts over the level of the sea. Drink a lot of water and move slowly. If you feel bad some aspirins will help. Temperature is very low - 8 degrees in celsius. When you get to the spot its kind of dark so you will be able to see the sun rise in the middle of the Andes. Beautiful They will give you breakfast and after that they will show you the geysers. Very cool. After a 100 mt hike you will get to the thermal pool. You can swim there for 30 minutes. It sounds a bit crazy considering low temperature but its worthy. Do it, you wont regret. You leave the place heading to Rio Putana. A short stop there to take pictures of tha flora and fauna of the place. After that you get to a small town called Machuca. Please try their food. Specially fried empanadas stuffed with goat cheese and "Llama anticuchos". An anticucho its wooden stick where they put chopped meat and onions and they cook them in a grill heated with coal. Outstanding flavour!!! Then you leave Machuca straight to San Pedro and thats the end of the tour. Did it through Altiplano Aventura agency. Again I must say that the guide, Arturo and the driver Ruben, they rock!! Do this trip through and ahency, roads to Tatio are rough.

review_text: We're just back from a Sept week in Portillo, and we enjoyed it. The warm Chilean sun, the spring corn snow, the friendliness of everyone we met, the good food and wine, and seeing the Canadian ski team and US women's team train, all combined for a great week. Most of my group wants to return. As North Americans, we appreciated the opportunity to ski at this time of year! We also appreciated how well we were treated. We wished we could do more off-piste skiing but understand we need to come earlier in the season to catch fresh powder. The resort's guest rooms need some refurbishing -- think 1970s European sports hotel, but the rooms are clean, and the common areas were just fine. The scene was international and fun. The hotel had a great band in the bar for 2 of the nights we were there. The other nights also had live music. Some of us did a one day snowshoe trek at the base of Mt. Aconcagua with a guide (booked in the hotel). I highly recommend this excursion. The scenery was breathtaking.

review_text: I did the "Tatio geysers" and "Lagunas Antiplanicas" tours with my girlfriend, and both of them are a must do at San Pedro de Atacama. Even though it can be a little more expensive, if you take more than a tour, you will may get discounts, and apart from that, it is totally worth it. When we arrived at the agency, we had the pleasure to meet Inés, who was very nice to us and gave me a lot of information and tips about the tours. Then troughout the two tours Santiago, the guide, and Alfredo, the driver, formed an excellent team and made the tours to be an outstanding experience. They gave us a lot of information, and were all the time trying to make the most out of the tour. Both of them prepared breakfast for us, they were concerned about every detail of it ( it was cooked there in the middle of the desert in a grill they have) and it was delicious. It included panqueques, toasted sandwiches, coffee, etc. It is important to mention that the truck is very comfortable,and since the tour starts around 5 am, it is great for sleeping until the trip to the first stop. Oh and they give you blankets for staying warm!

review_text: We (2 adults and 2 teen aged children) just returned, (yesterday) from a two week trip to Chile, all arrangements made by Cascada. I couldn't wait even one day to rave about the brilliant job they (Cecelia) did with our itinerary. We flew to Punta Arenas where we were met at the airport and transported to town. The town is small but we found several nice restaurants and it functions mostly as a gateway to the Patagonia region. We were picked up and transported by small bus to the Ecocamp office in Puerto Natales, where we were given lunch in a nearby restaurant (good meatless options) before continuing to the camp in Torres del Paine. Torres del Paine is absolutely beautiful; the Ecocamp is clean and the guides are great. There were always meatless options, and the food was very good. We had three great, full day, treks on the amazing "W" circuit. Following our stay at Ecocamp, Cecelia booked us on a 3 day sea kayak trip through the southern part of the park. (specifically along the Serrano river). We camped and utilized one Hosteria in the most remote and beautiful locations. This is camping in the wilderness; oh so beautiful. We did not have a lot of sea kayak experience but our guide was fantastic and very patient. (this is a strenuous and very rewarding trip). This part of our trip concluded with 2 nights in Puetro Natales at the IF hotel. Puerto Natales is a very small (also gateway) town. There are good restaurants and out hotel was clean and comfortable. When our flight time was changed (on Christmas eve); the hotel called Cascada to arrange for a change in our airport pick up. We flew out of PN on Sky airlines. I think there are only a few flights a day, but this is a good option which I would recommend. Every transport was on time, all hotels were great; Cascada did an amazing job with our entire itinerary. We continued on to Pucon in the lake region; where, again, all accommodations were exactly as we had hoped. (including car rental pick up on New Year's Day) The entire trip went with out a hitch (amazing). I can't thank Cecelia and Cascada enough for making this trip possible. I couldn't wait even one day to rave about the brilliant job they (Cecelia) did with our itinerary. We flew to Punta Arenas where we were met at the airport and transported to town. The town is small but we found several nice restaurants and it functions mostly as a gateway to the Patagonia region. We were picked up and transported by small bus to the Ecocamp office in Puerto Natales, where we were given lunch in a nearby restaurant (good meatless options) before continuing to the camp in Torres del Paine. Torres del Paine is absolutely beautiful; the Ecocamp is clean and the guides are great. There were always meatless options, and the food was very good. We had three great, full day, treks on the amazing "W" circuit. Following our stay at Ecocamp, Cecelia booked us on a 3 day sea kayak trip through the southern part of the park. (specifically along the Serrano river). We camped and utilized one Hosteria in the most remote and beautiful locations. This is camping in the wilderness; oh so beautiful. We did not have a lot of sea kayak experience but our guide was fantastic and very patient. (this is a strenuous and very rewarding trip). This part of our trip concluded with 2 nights in Puetro Natales at the IF hotel. Puerto Natales is a very small (also gateway) town. There are good restaurants and out hotel was clean and comfortable. When our flight time was changed (on Christmas eve); the hotel called Cascada to arrange for a change in our airport pick up. We flew out of PN on Sky airlines. I think there are only a few flights a day, but this is a good option which I would recommend. Every transport was on time, all hotels were great; Cascada did an amazing job with our entire itinerary. We continued on to Pucon in the lake region; where, again, all accommodations were exactly as we had hoped. (including car rental pick up on New Year's Day) The entire trip went with out a hitch (amazing). I can't thank Cecelia and Cascada enough for making this trip possible. I would strongly recommend using them for travel anywhere in Chile. Hola, Thanks for your comments. We are delighted to know you had a once-in-a-lifetime experience with Cascada and that you enjoyed the quality of the services provided at EcoCamp. We are proud to work with such a sustainable and guest-friendly destination. Every guest feels at home "far away from home" at EcoCamp and our staff is dedicated to making our guests feel as comfortable as possible in the wilderness of Patagonia. We hope to welcome you again in Chile! Best, Timothy

review_text: We did two tours with this company - the first we had booked months in advance via Tempo Tours from home and the second we booked upon arrival into Chile before we had done the first. Our first tour was the city tour of Santiago. We got picked up at 8am, driven to a central depot where we didn't leave until 9:20am! Our bus driver joked about how we were running late again, as they did every single day. I double checked with a staff member in the pick up car on the way to the depot what time the tour should finish that afternoon as it was advertised as 3 hours. I was told that we should we back at our hotel by 12 - 12.30. Due to leaving so late, our tour still had 2 stops to go at 12.15 so we had to ask to be dropped back to our hotel because we had another tour booked for pick up at 2pm and we wanted to have lunch in between. They kindly obliged and dropped us back on the way to the next stop at about 1230 which was good of them but meant that we missed 2 stops due to the poor time management of the company. The tour of the city was a mixture of bus and walking. We saw some of the main sites including the main square, the president residence, the cathedral & got to see the changing of the guards. My husband and I were the only English speaking. The other 10 or so guests were Spanish speaking so our tour guide gave them the majority of attention. He also didn't speak great English so it was difficult for him to understand our questions. There was one time where I had to repeat my question to him multiple times. He then got another member of the group who spoke English as a second language to help translate and then provided a really unhelpful, minimal answer and moved on. At one stage, my husband asked a question about Pinochet to which he said 'I don't have time to explain, sorry'. He easily could have taken a couple of mins during our bus ride home later in the day. The next day, on a different tour with a different company, our guide provided a great short explanation of the history of Pinochet without even being prompted which answered his very question. Later on, we did the second tour with them. It was a winery tour so it was fine because the guide and entire tour experience was facilitated by the winery and not TurisTours. They simply picked us up from our hotel, took us to the depot again (no idea why they don't just pick people up from their hotels using the minibus in the first place?? I think they just want you to buy stuff at the 'depot' which doubles as a large, very expensive souvenir shop) where we only had about a 10-15 minute wait this time and were then driven to the winery where the tour was conducted and then we were brought back. Overall, I definitely would not rate this company - book through someone else!

review_text: after spending morning on our private colchagua valley wine tour, our guide dropped us off at the museum. my thinking was, oh no! "here's the fill in the gaps to justify a full day" what a surprise! the entrance is rather unassuming and the first impression is it looks very small, but, once you are inside, it goes on and on and eventually you realize there are numerous buildings and exhibit rooms. the short movie at the entrance is a must it you are unfamiliar with south american history and explains the museum's concepts and a brief history of the founder's passion for collecting the displayed items. from there, it is a fabulous journey of displays and items. of special interest to me were items that have been collected from the great south american empires (wari, mayan, incan, etc.) the only negative for me, was all the documentation and explanations are in spanish only.--- but, all in all, this is one of the most captivating museums i have ever been in.. allow several hours at a minimum.

review_text: An amazing trip from Punta Arenas to Ushuaia on the MV Stella Australis. Although it's billed as a 5 day cruise, you board on the evening of Day One and disembark on the morning of Day Five... so it's more like 3 full days, but the experience is completely worth it. You get to experience Patagonia and the extreme south of world up close with daily trips out on the zodiacs to glaciers, penguin colonies, Cape Horn and places of natural and historic interest. the boat has great accommodation and isn't too large (sleeps about 150 - 200 people) to feel overwhelming. We didn't see a single other boat or person the entire time we were there - it was like having the whole of the end of the world to yourself :-) Food and beverage was fine and generous and the guides were friendly and knowledgeable. If you're in Patagonia this is a 'must-do' experience!

review_text: In Pucón, everyone is raving about the volcano, overshadowing other worthwhile attractions. It is, indeed, a spectacular sight, especially from afar. But I was disappointed by the climb. First, because there is nothing to see on the way up : no secondary craters, no fumaroles... common on many volcanoes. Second, because the crater itself is quite small, although deep, so it's not overly impressive. And last, because the traditional way to go down - sliding on the snow - is extremely scary, although safer than walking down it seems. So I regret my 100 US dollars and those 3 hours spent climbing in the snow and loose scree. I do think one should try to go up, though - it is a unique experience. But don't go with too high expectations.

review_text: We booked 4 tours with whipala and we really enjoy the company and the service. - Valle de la Luna: the tour is very good, and Ernesto (our guide) told us a lot of information and explained a lot of things. We finish the tour with an amazing sunset - Laguna Cejar: was a nice and easy tour. We floated in one of the lagoons with a good view to the Licancabur. Javier was our guide and was very good. We would just escape the cocktail in the end. The days in the desert are very tiring, so we would rather arrive earlier at the hotel than have the cocktail - Geysers del Tatio: one of my favourite tours. Alex was a really good guide. We stopped halfway to acclimatize and we could see the sky full of stars. He told us a lot of tips to acclimating properly. The walk in the geysers was incredible! It was very impressive. In the end my boyfriend didn't feel so well and almost fainted and everyone was very kind with us. The breakfast was great and so the rest of the tour - Piedras Rojas: our favourite tour in Atacama! Javier was our guide again and he's really really good. He told us a lot of things. We went to laguna chaxa and saw a lot of flamingos. After we had an amazing breakfast on capricorn tropic. After that we went to piedras rojas, definitely the highlight of the day for us. We also stop in laguna miscanti with a nice view. We had lunch with at an amazing place. We were starving and was late but Javier explained us that this late lunch is because it's harder to have lunch and continuing to go up, so we totally understood. The pick up at the hotel for the early tours worked really well. The communication with the company as well. We would like to have done a stargazing tour and they were really honest saying thay the weather was not good for that. In resume, we think that Whipala is a great company to do the tours! They always text you the day before. They send you a message saying what you need to bring to the tour. Book with them!!!

review_text: We visited the alto plano and the lagoons as part of a full day excursion from the Explora lodge in San Pedro de Atacama. The scenery and location is breathtaking - partly because at 4000m above sea level there is a lot less oxygen in the air, but mainly because of the visual impact of the scenery. Beautiful lagoons dotted with flamingos, grazing llamas and other wildlife. Absolutely clear air so the surrounding high mountains seem much closer. The high desert landscape is so different from anything else I had experienced, what I would expect Mars to look like. We were there in June so it was quite cold, especially when the wind was blowing, but we were well prepared and very comfortable. Explora provided a really comfortable vehicle with driver and a very knowledgeable guide. They also provided a gourmet lunch which we enjoyed in a sheltered location with great views of the lagoon and mountains. Well worth the time and effort to visit!

review_text: Our first destination this morning was Pueblito Artesan Village at Los Dominicos. It is a assemblage of about 100 small clay and thatch-roofed huts and workshop shacks that house artists and craftsmen, located adjacent to the San Vincent Ferrer Parish Church that is a National Monument. A bus load of Australian tourists had arrived just before we did, but they were dispersed quickly among the many small shops and a couple cafes. It is a very warm and comfortable area to stone paths and overhanging trees. There were jewellers and potters, knitwear scarves and shawls and rugs, painters, artists working in copper and tin and leather, furniture makers and basket weavers. There were also small animal and bird sellers and three large enclosures containing many birds including peacocks and parakeets and all manner of brightly-coloured feathered flyers, and you could buy a cage at the same time to house them. We window-shopped and only purchased some Chilean spice.

review_text: We booked this tour via the Vacations to Go web site. Our tour was to depart on March 10, 2019 at 9 AM; we got in the tender line on the Holland America at 7:45 AM (tender tickets were given starting at 8 AM)but did not get off the ship and onto the pier until 9:45 AM. That was our mistake, not understanding how long it would take to get off the ship. We immediately found a guide we checked us in and told us to race after him. We ran and then were stopped by another woman who encouraged to go on the shuttle instead of the bus. We asked quick questions and found that she was with the same tour company and wanted $30/person more for the shuttle, so we quickly declined and raced toward the bus that took off without us. Consequently we raced back to the shuttle and were allowed on without an extra charge. We enjoyed the sites, but the guide provided very little narration. We asked her to increase her narration but she did not do so. We enjoyed seeing the waterfalls. The shops at the Petrohue waterfalls were most reasonable in price and quality but we had no time to shop as we spent our time at the falls. We also made a stop at an overlook to have our "snack" - some wine and empanades. When the snack was taken out, we were surrounded by bees and one stung my husband on the left side of his tongue leaving him with a swollen tongue and unable to speak and eat! We reported this to the guide and was offered water. Another site is recommended for a meat snack stop! Frutillar is not impressive but more history of the town would have been useful. All-in-all, this can be a very nice tour, but a better guide and consideration for guests is very important. We also will be mindful of how long it takes to get off a ship which uses tenders. review_text: There are four main ways to get to the statue of the virgin Mary at the top - furnicular railway from the west; cable car from the east; driving from the main entrance; or walking. We walked from the south but not from the main entrance. We eventually found the way to the top with the help of Google maps. The paths we used were shorter than walking up the roads and took just under an hour. Be careful as some 'paths' are actually mountain bike tracks. Also, if you rake the wrong path you can end up on completely the wrong ridge. From the top there are views of the city and the snow capped Andes behind. From here you can also really see the smog; apparently it is better after it has been raining but I don't know about that. We went twice as our hotel was very close and it was better early in the morning before the sun was too hot. There is a small shop at the top but I would recommend taking some water. There are toilets but we didn't use them. There is also a small church with amazing stone carvings on the interior walls. Definitely worth the climb (or pesos for the train/gondola).

review_text: This was a 5 star experience all the way. We cannot praise Thomas Poussard, our tour guide Vincent and his company Chile Private Tours enough. Our cruise ship Celebrity Infinity arrived in Valpariso in the early morning hours of December 24. Our plane back to Atlanta wasn't until 10 that night. Then late in the day when we were all exhausted, Vincent and the driver dropped all of us and our luggage at the Santiago Airport for our trip back to the U.S. What a wonderful day and tremendous climax to our 15 day trip to South America.

review_text: Based on this experience I can recommend Turistik tours. Picked up at 8:15am from hotel, in mini-bus taken to back of shopping mall at Las Condes where the Turistik buses merge and you join the correct on for your chosen tour - organised and works like clockwork. Luckily the bus I was on was the one for this tour so stayed seated. Left around 9:15 and due to time of year, the wine tasting was first on the stop-off at around 11:30. Matetic vineyard is beautifully surrounded by hills and vines (obviously) and is an organic producer - quality over quantity. There were 9 people on this tour and a perfect size for being shown around by our guide. Tasting at the end of a white and a red, very small gift shop here. Then just a short ride to Matetics own boutique hotel/restaurant for lunch (price not included in tour) but you will want to eat here - looks like it is going to be out of price range but I found it reasonable and probably the best meal I had in Chile this year !! Probably around £25 for the 2 courses with a glass of their wine The surrounding is beautifully presented and there is a boutique hotel they own too. After lunch just a short trip to the coast and Isla Negra to Pablo Neurda's house (see separate review) Then back to Santiago mall, before coaches take you back to your hotel Excellent throughout our bus driver Rodrigo and guide Cristima, would definitely try a different tour with these guys next time. review_text: Although we have some suggestions for improvement of this tour, this still was the highlight of our trip. What better way to earn our wine than by biking through a huge, beautiful vineyard at the base of the Andes? Our tour guide, Philippe, was outstanding and very considerate with us English speakers. He went above and beyond to ensure we were comfortable, informed, and having a good time. He gave us a history of the region on the way to the vineyard (around 40 minutes) and in no time, we had our bikes and were off to tour. The vineyard was flat ground, and although the bikes had gears, they were not needed. We rode around for about an hour or so (no wine at this point!) and then got a mini-tour of the winery. Very interesting. Would've been more interesting if we were sampling the wine that we were talking about :) We then biked over to a pretty spot and heard more about the history of the grapes and the region and Philippe opened a bottle for all of us to taste. Very idyllic! Then we rode back to the winery for the official tasting. Although informative and intimate (photo attached), we felt pretty rushed during our extremely short wine tasting. We sampled three provided wines that we did not choose and then we had about 15 minutes in the store to purchase the wines. We received assistance and they bubble-wrapped our wines for us since we we planned to put them in our suitcase. My husband and I liked the fact that this was not an all-day tour, but the fact that pick-up was at 8:15 am and no food was provided was brutal for us night-life lovers. We knew they weren't going to provide food, but since we spent the morning biking and then drinking by about 11:30, a light snack or time to stop at the cafe would've been perfect. Overall, quick and fun way to learn about Chilean wine and see the vineyards, but lacking on the actual wine tasting. We thank you for all your comments. We will consider each of them to improve our service. We want to make our experience memorable. We hope back to his country has many fond memories of our walk. We hope to see you again soon. Turistik Team

review_text: Breathtaking landscapes! We stayed in Puerto Natales (Pousada Trotamundos), We rented a car (Tom rent a car), and visited the park for three days. We went to Mirador Base das Torres, Blue Laguna, Amarga Laguna, Mirador Nordenskjold, Mirador Cuernos, Salto Grande, Mirador Pehoe, Mirador Condor, and Lake Gray. All very good, but I highlight the base of the Towers, Cuernos and Condor. To make the base view of the towers has to be well prepared, we did all the route in 9h (1h at the base), has two stops both with bathroom and water, and the first stop has snack options and drinks. Important to be with the right clothing, waterproof trekking shoes, thermal clothing, waterproof and wind cut. Taking the Gray Lake, which is closest to Portaria Serrano, the other points suggest going through the entrance of the Amarga Laguna because the access to the entrance is all asphalt despite being further away from the city, but still worth it.

review_text: Ben was an amazing host for our first day exploring the Torres del Paines region. He gave my husband some instruction, set him on the river to fish and then gave me, a total beginner, a 1 on 1 casting lesson in the field! Once I got some good casting down, we moved to the river and continued learning and casting, all in the most idyllic area. We moved up stream after every few casts so we were always seeing something new. We caught 7 fish that day between the two of us and Ben actually jumped chest deep into the river to help us net a big Sea Run trout that had pulled into the weeds. Ben was genuinely excited every time we got a bites it was so fun!! Then for lunch he set up quite the display! He shielded our lunch from the wind with his car. Had smoked salmon and beef, quinoa and fruit, red wine, white wine, beer, coke, and bottled water. Then we fished for hours more. I was tentative about the cost but afterwards I had no qualms about how much we spent to have one of the best days of our lives. Thanks Ben!

review_text: We did the W Trek from west to east. A park ranger came onto the bus when we entered the park and told us that the catamaran wasn't running that day but that it was going to be replaced by small boats - so far so good. It was only when we'd already got to Pudeto (and the bus we took in had already left) that we found out (from other hikers, not the rangers or anyone who worked at the park) that the small boat could only take 20 people an hour... and we had about 80 people in front of us in the queue. If we'd just known before we got off the bus we could've stayed on to hike from Administracion or got the other boat from Hotel Grey with time to spare, but instead we had to piece together the situation from other hikers, pay the driver of the one remaining bus an extra 5.000 CLP to drive us to Administracion and try to make the 5 hour hike in 4 hours in order to get to Paine Grande before the trail to Refugio Grey closed. If anything we got lucky - apparently when the small boat ran out of passengers in Paine Grande to ferry on the return trip they just stopped running it and told everyone still on the wharf to walk to Administracion and then to Paine Grande (eta 10 hours... starting at 3pm). The leftovers who didn't take the bus back to Puerto Natales had to hitchhike to Administracion, start hiking and get to Paine Grande at 9pm. Cheekily, the ticket office was even handing out catamaran timetables with the park tickets despite knowing it wasn't running. I guess whoever owns the catamaran was still pretty keen on collecting their 22.000 CLP fare even if it meant stranding a few dozen trekkers. Just getting in costs 20.000 CLP and it's not entirely clear where the money is going... trails except the main Hotel Torres -> Torres Del Paine route are poorly marked, bridges are falling apart or poorly signposted (many have signs with the maximum number of people on them... but only on one side of the bridge!?), the map will tell you to be sure to register yourself on each sector of the trek but we only ever saw a single registration book the whole time. Then there's the refugios - some are better than others, but they're all insanely overpriced. It's easy to think "it's worth it to be in this amazing place", but there is a point at which it's not worth it anymore, and 240USD per night to sleep in a tent and eat boiled eggs for breakfast is way beyond that point. The genius of the refugios is that they're so insanely difficult to book that by the time you get given the price, you're so grateful to have gotten any response that you'll pay anything. It's a beautiful place - but the ridiculous prices you'll pay for every single thing, the obvious lack of reinvestment of that money back into the park, and the general lack of any care given by anyone who works there leaves a pretty sour taste in the mouth. There are other beautiful places in the world where you aren't left feeling like the mark in a con job - go there first.

review_text: World class fly fishing on a variety of rivers and lakes. Natural beauty beyond anything that I have ever seen. Glacers, blue green water, mountains, valleys, lakes, and rivers so beautiful it takes your breath away and makes you cry. It’s a place where my cup runneth over and it restored my soul. Five star meals prepared by Chef Carolina, the finest chef in Chile, and served with fine Chilean wines. First Class Lodging on the bank of the Rio Futilafu with beautiful snowcap mountains and meadows all around. Our guide, Nick Lawton, provided ten days of fly fishing on rivers and lakes that were varied in their challenges, beauty, and techniques. Walking and Wading, drift boats, and trolling for big trout on two spectacular lakes. Gourmet stream side lunches with table and chairs, homemade hot chili, grilled sausages, potato salad, and grilled skewers of beef/vegetables. Nick navigated the boat back and forth across streams, lakes, and through fast water with the greatest of ease. He shared many techniques on flies, knots, strategy, casting, and where the fish feed. He shared many stories of his incredible life as fly fishing guide around the world. Nick, Carolina, and his staff worked so hard from first light till late night insuring that every detail was covered from equipment, gear, clothing, glasses, food, and so much more. It was truly a privilege to get to know this crew and to have experienced the most wonderful vacation of my life. I will keep a place in my heart for all of them and all of the Chilean people that I met on this trip. They are all so beautiful and such great ambassadors of Chile. And to Nick’s partner, Avear, I say Ol Boy! Stephen, Thank you so much for taking the time to write this review. We appreciate your feedback and thoroughly enjoyed sharing the real Patagonia fly fishing experience with you. We are very pleased to know that you enjoyed your trip with us. Chef Carolina and the whole crew really enjoyed your company and we look forward to the opportunity to share this experience with you next season. Saludos

review_text: When I visited San Pedro I thought we had to take a tour to the Geyser del Tatio, but I am so glad we did not do it. We started driving from San Pedro around 8 am. Yes, maybe sunrise at this place would have been stunning, but it is stunning anyway, seeing the geyser with the clear blue skies and the Andes mountains in the distance. So colorful. I have one regret and that is that I did not take my bathing suite, as there is a small hot pool. The road is reasonable. couple of huge pot holes, but overall good to drive. I would not do it in the darkness. So if you want to see the sunrise you need to take a tour. But as I said I loved the drive, we saw lots of animals, even a fox. Dont expect any luxury. review_text: Recently I had a chance to visit my son in Chile who was spending 6 months studying as an exchange student at the Chilean Naval Academy. Having limited time to spend in Chile, I booked at the last minute a tour with Al Ramirez Wine Tours . Big mistake. Our tour guide was not familiar with wines and actually said he preferred beer to wine. Half way through the tour, I also realized the tour guide was taking us on the wrong tour. When I brought this to his attention, He ended the tour and said I was to pay extra if I wanted the tour to continue. At the end, Our tour guide was also very unfamiliar on how to accept our payment of cash. If you take this tour, be prepared to pay extra cost not being told about and having a guide who knows nothing about wine. At Valparaiso Wine Tours, we work with bookings which are carried out 48 hours ahead of time. This person was doing things last minute and the wineries she wanted to visit were not taking the reservation, and unfortunately she didn't like the Indomita Winery. So, I offered her a refund for the OPTIONAL (meaning not included) winery, where she had to spend $20 USD per person for a tour. Thats's what this complaint is about. The whole thing about the guide not being a wine lover or things being unclear in the email... if anyone writes me an email, everything is crystal clear in the first response. If the guide says he is a lover of beer more than wine is because he makes beer and not wine! but that doesn't mean he can't be a wine lover; that shouldn't even be in this complaint. Also, we include two wineries, and the third is optional. If you don't want a thrid winery, we can return to your hotel. If you want to have lunch, we can take you to lunch... everyone, since 2009, when that route was created, has understood this, but this person obviously didn't take the time to read the tour description. We had over 150 clients that week and not one group was dissatisfied, except for this one, and obviously if you book last minute, the premium wineries will not be expecting you with a red carpet. And finally, there were three people in that group, and two out of three did not have a compalint; in fact they thanked the guide for a great day.

review_text: NOTE: Our visit was actually Feb 2017 (summer in South America) If your time is limited, you can see a good bit of the park in one day, but to really experience it, you should stay either in the park or close by. We took a bus tour from El Calafate leaving at 7 am and returning at 9 pm. The bus was comfortable and we stopped at a local souvenir store on the return trip for expensive snacks (if you wanted them). A sack lunch was included in the tour. Arriving from Argentina, we had to stop at the border and pay for our Chilean visas. (It is better to use American or Chilean money; the exchange rate for Argentinian pesos is terrible.) The iconic Blue Towers (Torres del Paine) are tucked in a massif in the middle of the park. Our route took us around a good bit of the massif, but we were always viewing the towers from a great distance as the road is in the surrounding plains and foothills. Our first stops were two lakes and a beautiful waterfall overlook where we ate our sack lunches and stretched our legs. Farther down the road we encountered a guanaco herd and got out to take photos. We enjoyed a 2-hour leisurely stroll to a view of the Horns across a lake and then to another waterfall. (It was not a strenuous walk, but is a dirt path.) It was a full day and I was left wishing we could have stayed overnight at least. I imagine the towers can be quite dramatic in changing light. (Clouds rested on them most of the day.) One couple on our bus took their luggage and was staying in a cabin. There was also a camping area with many backpackers. Our tour was organized by Say Hueque and the guides on the bus and in the park were excellent.

review_text: Our Chiloe Natural tour was a highlight of the various port/shore excursions we took during our recent South America/Antarctica cruise. Cyril is a knowledgeable, articulate guide whose funny stories and passion for Chiloe made this a memorable day and we particularly liked being part of a small group of four rather than a tour bus of forty. With the limited time allowed by the cruise stop, we enjoyed a variety of experiences - the unusual cemetary in Huillinco and the view over the lake, the Chiloe National Park visitor's centre and Tepual hike, Cyril's description of folklore, plants and birds. Cyril took extra time to drive us to see the magnificent 25k beach although this wasn't part of the official itinerary. It was on my wish list and I appreciated that he accommodated my request. In Chonchi, we enjoyed our lunch stop at Ventanas de Elisa, the market, the accordian museum and visiting the UNESCO church, with the explanation of the architectural restoration and how churches are the hub of community activities. Due to some techinical glitches, we found it somewhat challenging to book the tour, because we had difficulty arranging the PayPal deposit, however, we are very glad that we were able to make the booking. Highly recommended!

review_text: This was my first experience with real snow, and it was unforgettable. Much of it was thanks to our guide, Luciano, and driver, Mario. They were extremely kind and attentive. The road to the park includes 40 very steep curves, which might make some people feel sick. During our tour, a little girl felt uneasy and Luciano and Mario were perfect: they looked for a safe place to make a stop, attended to the little girl's family, and only when everything was OK, they summarized the road. Luciano gave clear instructions about the park attractions, and food facilities and was reachable throughout the entire time. Mario was a careful driver, both going up and down the mountain. They also left us closer to our hotel than the original endpoint and gave us clear instructions to return. The park is organized, ideal for kids of all ages, and perfect if you have no experience with snow sports, but want to learn. Restrooms were clean, and there was room for people who wanted to rest. There are food trucks all along the park and even my husband, who needs a gluten-free meal could find something to eat. There are attractions for everyone, excellent infrastructure, and a gorgeous place. The only thing I would change is the loud music in the main attraction area. It is unnecessary, and prevents you from listening to the sounds of nature (but that's my personal opinion). Will definitely be back! review_text: My husband and I just did kayaking and glacier trekking with Big Foot, and had two incredible experiences. Both activities were well organized and we felt safe the entire time. I could not believe the amount of gear we were given for kayaking, but certainly kept us warm! We kayaked through ice bergs and had great views of Glacier Grey. I must say though if you could only choose one activity, the glacier trekking was one of the most incredible experiences we had ever had. The whole experience was about 5 hours - we took a 10 minute boat ride and then a short hike to the glacier, where put on our crampons before climbing up. We had 6 people in our group and were mostly inexperienced, and our guides were fantastic and helpful. They took us out pretty far too - we must have hiked about 3 miles, and did not see a single other soul out there. Perfect way to end our experience on the W trek, and can't recommend this company highly enough.

review_text: I cannot speak highly enough of Antilco. My boyfriend and I visited Chile in November, 2011 for 5 days. I am an avid horse back rider with over 20 years of experience riding and training in the US. I love riding in other countries, but I am a stickler for safety, good horsemanship, and EXCELLENT horse care. I will not hesitate to walk out of an establishment that is lax about safety or the well being of their mounts. Antilco was FANTASTIC. Way beyond my expectations. When we arrived, I was happy to see a string of very well cared for Chilean horses (healthy well trimmed hooves, clean shiny well groomed coats, appropriate weight, and excellent muscle tone on ALL their horses) hanging out calmly in a clean shaded paddock with access to hay and water. Further, none of the horses had that "dead- eyed" look of being overworked. They were all alert and interactive with their humans, seemed to enjoy their jobs, and moved out easily away from the barn with no hint of the "barn sour"-ness that unfortunately happens to so many overworked trail horses. The healthy horses were followed by a neatly arranged tack room with well conditioned bridles and saddles in good repair and (much to my joy as I didn't have any gear with me)... half chaps! Another good sign: nearly all the bridles have gentle snaffle bits or hackamores, indicating very well trained horses with happy mouths! :) It was pouring rain the day we rode, but they provided rain ponchos as well, in part to keep the riders happy and in part to help keep the 30- some layers of wool in their incredible saddles dry (more on the saddles to follow). Antilco also provides ASTM approved helmets to anyone who wants one. Our guide was extremely friendly and a very knowledgeable and accomplished horseman (I believe he was German?, but spoke impeccable English and Spanish). He spoke with everyone briefly and easily matched up the guests to appropriate horses. My boyfriend has ridden a grand total of 4 times in his life, so when we travel, it is imperative for me to find a trekking company that will provide him with a safe mount, not only so he doesn't get hurt, but also so I can keep him happy enough to continue riding with me on our vacations :P Our guide at Antilco did an excellent job assigning horses. After a brief warmup walk on the trail, our guide announced we were going to canter up the hill on the road. I panicked thinking "there is NO WAY my boyfriend can canter! He barely knows how to steer or stop!" But my fears were quickly allayed when his horse slowly and carefully picked up a gentle rolling lope and followed the others up the hill without so much as coming close to unbalancing my boyfriend and totally unaffected by my boyfriend bouncing awkwardly a bit on his back. I wish I could remember the name of his horse, because that fantastic animal deserves some kind of medal or at least a few extra carrots :) My horse was lively and moved forward easily, but was also very calm with excellent response to all my aids, something I really did not expect in a career trail horse, who, in the US at least, typically walk nose to tail and ignore anything the rider asks for. He was really a pleasure to ride. Another helpful thing for beginner riders (or anyone going on a long, multiday trek): the Chilean saddles are like COUCHES! I'm an eventing rider and used to shallow seated English saddles. These were the exact opposite. I'm pretty sure it would be impossible to fall off of one. It felt like I would literally have to dive off the side of my horse to come loose. They are WAY deeper seated and more secure even than any Western style American saddle I've ever sat in. Although this was a really strange feeling for me, the saddles are extremely comfortable and PERFECT for an inexperienced rider who needs a really secure saddle to handle some of the tougher terrain encountered on the trail. They were comfortable enough that my boyfriend, who is usually sore and tired after a couple hours, was able to ride for 4 hours with little complaint. We rode for about 2 hours on trails and back roads, through the woods, the mountains, and several traditional villages. The ride is not simply a "nose to tail" follow along on a flat road (nor was it too difficult for beginners). There was plenty of trotting and cantering and lots of varying terrain. There were also 2 challenging, rocky creek crossings that those amazing little Chilean horses handled beautifully. They are SO surefooted and fit! We stopped in a sheep field, tied the horses to some trees, and had a lovely lunch provided by Antilco (vegetarian options available!). Then we remounted and headed back by a different route that included a nice (optional!) gallop on a volcanic sand beach. And finally, the scenery is AMAZING. The small taste of Patagonia we got on this half day trail, and the excellent experience with Antilco, has made me think very seriously about returning for a week long trek. I really cannot say enough good things about their guides and their horses. Such a fantastic experience!

review_text: We had a layover of approx 7 hrs in Santiago. What to do? This is it. We got a taxi into town and picked up the afternoon tour. You can bus or shuttle but we wanted to save time. We paid $40 USD for our taxi but coming back it was only $30 on advise of the guide. We arrived at 12.45 and by 1.35 had cleared customs and were at Plaza de Armus. It was great to find a person so passionate about the history of his city/county and so knowledgable. It was such a relaxing walk after being cooped up in a plane for long hours. You stop about every 5 min to learn something new. Unfortutunately we had to leave the tour early (around 6.15) but the tour was to continue for about another 45 min. It was still worth the tip (we gave 15000 peso for 2 people) and felt we received excellent value for money. If planning to spend longer in Santiago we agree with previous viewers that this tour is an excellent introduction to exploring Santiago at your leisure. Note that it does cost to leave the airport even if only on a layover but it was so much better than sitting in an airport.

Every detail was outlined and the tour went just as planned. I planned a free day in Pucon before the tour started. Stef arranged all of the logistics as well as adding an extra day to my tour for me personally. Stef also went out of her way to seek me out at the hotel, making sure I was taken care of and even invited me to come hiking with another tour. The day the tour started I was picked up by my guide, Dave, and Bernardo, our driver. My tour was a hiking and biking one and I am so glad I mixed it up. I'm an avid cyclist and South America was my 5th continent to ride! The rides were fantastic and the geology and scenery of the region are amazing. You must climb the VILLARICCA VOLCAN. The accommodations were perfect. And based on my research the VALUE of this tour far exceeded other tours I found. Pucon is a lovely tourist town. And the Chilenos, their preferred word for natives, are as friendly a people as I have ever been around. I would HIGHLY recommend Amity Tours without reservation. Let me expand. The measure of a tour company is not how they perform when things go as planned, but rather when things don't go as planned. It was completely my fault that on the last day of the group tour I caught a pothole, a real big one. The bike is fine, but at the end of the day I ended up with a multitude of rib fractures as well as fractures to my clavicle and scapula. As soon as possible Bernardo and Dave rushed me to the local Pucon hospital. Dave and Bernardo stayed with me for hours until I was safe and secure in my room. Dave visited me twice during my 5 day stay. After 2 hospitals and 5 nights, 2 scans and several X-rays my total bill was ZERO! Amity's insurance covered it all. Additionally I have never received better medical services anywhere, even in my own USA. The Amity owners and employees are awesome. The tour was spectacular. Amity really came through when I needed them and was all alone in a foreign country.

review_text: An early morning visit is the best time since the contrast in the air and water temperatures generates the most steam. As the air temperature warms there is considerably less water vapour visible. The geysers are an hour and a half to two hours drive from San Pedro de Atacama. This is a popular attraction and there will be lots of people around. However, the geyser field is big enough that we could enjoy the spectacle. It is cold. Dress for the snow and you will be able to enjoy the majestic setting and take your time exploring the many different hot water pools. Some bubble, others just breathe out steam. There is a swimming pool sized thermal pool, with changing rooms, for anyone brave enough to undress in the chilling cold. If you're not on an organised tour take food and drink since there's nowhere to buy anything. Entry to the geysers is about 5000 pesos (cash) and may not be included in the cost of a guided tour. On the way back to San Pedro we saw a surprising variety of animal: vicuña, rabbits, wild donkeys and a red fox.

review_text: My husband and I hiked the W at the end of March 2014. We booked everything ourselves. I'll provide a report based on components of the trip, which is likely to be most helpful for those planning the hike for themselves. Transportation: We didn't book any of the ground transportation to or from the park in advance, and this worked fine. When I arrived in Punta Arenas, I went straight to Bus Fernandez and booked our bus tickets to Puerto Natales for the following morning. We were then able book the bus to the park when we arrived at Puerto Natales, and so on. Don't bother paying a company to book all the transfers for you - you'll only pay more than you need and it's so easy to arrange on the ground. Accommodation: We stayed in refugios every night (Refugio Torres 2 nights, a cabana at Cuernos, Paine Grande and Lodge Grey) and were glad we did. The wind is blustering in the park and it was wet a few days of the trip and we would have been miserable if we had to set up tents in this and try to sleep through the wind. We even saw some tents had blown away! We booked beds without sheets, so took our own sleeping bags and this saved a bit of cash. Food: We booked full board at every refugio. We are good eaters with solid appetites, but it was consistently too much food for both of us. I recommend buying your first dinner in Puerto Natales from the supermarket and taking it with you into the park - I saw a group who'd brought in a roast chicken with salad and bread rolls, and it looked better than what we were eating in the refugio (and probably cheaper). Dinner most nights was rice with meat and a very salty gravy/sauce. Vegetables were scarce. I didn't like the food much, it was too salty for me.
